JOB TITLE: Logistics Analyst

REPORTS TO: Global Director of Supply Chain & Logistics

STATUS: Fulltime, Exempt

LOCATION: Remote – East Coast

SALARY: $85,000 - $100,000/year based on interview outcome & overall experience

BENEFITS:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance, optional FSA/HSA, 401k with 6% employer match, life and AD&D insurance, Employee Assistance Program, short & long-term disability, tuition reimbursement, 21.67 days of paid time off + 10 holidays

About Tidal Vision:

We believe that sustainability should not require customers to compromise on price, convenience, or performance. Our mission is to create positive and systemic environmental impact by making our biopolymer solutions cost competitive, more convenient, and better performing than the synthetic chemicals we displace. We value innovation and take pride in challenging the status-quo; we choose to view obstacles as opportunities. We value new ideas and encourage the team to apply creativity and invent new solutions to meet challenging demands. We foster open, direct communication, and a collaborative working environment through our unique approach to work culture. We value our employees and demonstrate that through our compensation and benefits programs and opportunities for growth and development.

About Our Unique Work Culture:

Tidal Vision strives to build and invest in the highest performing and most innovative team. We put our people and customers above process, avoid company-wide rules as much as possible, and have the courage to take unusual approaches to advance our mission. With this approach, we believe we can create a more flexible, fun, stimulating, creative, collaborative, and innovative organization.

Our commitment to developing, practicing and promoting direct and open communication, responsibility and freedom, and leading with and seeking context is a responsibility for every role at Tidal Vision.

Job Summary:

The Logistics Analyst manages the movement of goods into, out of, and across the U.S. About half the role is international: booking ocean and air exports with freight forwarders, preparing export documents, and clearing imports through customs with the customs broker. The other half is domestic: scheduling, tracking, and managing carrier performance for truckload (TL), less-than-truckload (LTL), and bulk liquid tank truck shipments.

Essential Job Functions

International exports (ocean and air)

  • Obtain and compare rates from freight forwarders for ocean and air export shipments.
  • Book shipments with the selected forwarder and confirm cutoffs, sailing or flight schedules, and delivery commitments.
  • Prepare and process all export documents, including the Shipper's Letter of Instruction (SLI), commercial invoice, and packing list, and send them to the freight forwarder.
  • Confirm export classification and filing details (Schedule B/HTS codes, ECCN, EEI filing in AES) are accurate.
  • Coordinate dangerous goods documentation and labeling for hazardous shipments with the forwarder.

International imports

  • Manage all imports into the U.S. from booking through delivery.
  • Work with the customs broker to clear goods through U.S. Customs, providing accurate commercial invoices, packing lists, and classification information.
  • Track inbound shipments and resolve customs holds, exams, and documentation issues.

Domestic transportation

  • Schedule truckload (TL), less-than-truckload (LTL), and bulk liquid tank truck shipments.
  • Track shipments from pickup through delivery and communicate delays to customers, production, and planning.
  • Monitor carrier performance on on-time pickup and delivery, damage, and cost.
  • Obtain carrier quotes and select carriers based on cost, service, and capability.
  • Schedule shipments on the company's private fleet of tankers and tractors when it is the better option than a third-party carrier.

Reporting and compliance

  • Maintain accurate shipment records and documentation for audits and compliance.
  • Process and approve freight invoices for international and domestic shipments, reviewing them against quotes and resolving discrepancies.
  • Report on freight costs, carrier performance, and shipment status to management.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, International Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 4–5+ years in logistics, with hands-on experience in both international and domestic shipping.
  • Experience booking ocean and air exports through freight forwarders and preparing export documentation, including the SLI.
  • Experience working with customs brokers to clear U.S. imports.
  • Working knowledge of Incoterms, Schedule B/HTS classification, and EEI filing requirements.
  • Experience scheduling and managing TL and LTL carriers.
  • Strong Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, basic reporting) and proficiency with Word and Outlook.
  • Clear, firm written and verbal communication with forwarders, brokers, carriers, and internal teams.
  • High attention to detail, documentation discipline, and follow-through on open items.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience shipping bulk liquids by tank truck.
  • Experience shipping chemicals or other hazardous materials, with dangerous goods training or certification (49 CFR, IATA, IMDG).
  • Familiarity with export controls (EAR/ECCN) and Importer Security Filing (ISF).
  • Experience using NetSuite or a transportation management system (TMS).
  • Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) or Certified Export Specialist (CES) credential.
  • Experience with private fleet management or scheduling a private fleet alongside third-party carriers, including familiarity with DOT/FMCSA requirements.

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements:

  • Minimal travel required (as needed for key meetings or project support). Estimated 5%-10%.
  • Time split – 50% International, 50% domestic
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use a computer and standard office tools.
  • The employee may occasionally visit industrial or customer sites and should be comfortable in those environments.

Licensing & Special Requirements:

  • The incumbent is subject to background check.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

jobs.description:
EMPLOYER IS A CONTRACTOR FOR THE U.S. GOVERNMENT. THIS POSITION REQUIRES U.S. CITIZENSHIP.

Role Description

We are seeking a talented and experienced Platform Engineer to join our team. Possessing strong proficiency with Kubernetes, the ideal candidate will play a crucial role in the development and maintenance of our platform, demonstrating a strong understanding of system architecture, problem-solving skills, and the ability to guide junior engineers.

As a Platform Engineer within our organization, you will join a team of dedicated unicorns who are focused on advancing freedom and independence globally. Our teams work on various different technical baselines depending on specific engagements. We focus our Products on the Platform layer, but to deliver for our Heroes, we also work IaC automation, security, and implementation.

Responsibilities

You will help us automate and build a runtime Production Environment and serve as a link between the Applications, either custom development, COTS, or OSS, and that environment, advocating best practices and facilitating communication between the application teams and platform teams.

In this position, you will be expected to:

  • Validate Solutions/Implementations: Ensure that solutions and implementations align with the outlined tasks and business requirements. Conduct thorough validations to maintain the integrity and efficiency of the platform.
  • Independently Problem Solve: Demonstrate the ability to identify and solve business problems independently. Develop small components to address specific challenges without relying on explicit architecture diagrams.
  • Understand Medium-Level Tasking: Comprehend how medium-level tasks contribute to the achievement of overall goals. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate various components into a cohesive and functional platform.
  • Estimate Time and Effort: Provide accurate time and effort estimates for medium-sized tasks. Assist in project planning and resource allocation based on estimated timelines.
  • Demonstrate Programming Language Proficiency: Possess familiarity with at least one programming language. Exhibit a basic understanding of when to use a programming language versus a shell for efficient task execution.
  • Own the Bridge Between Application Development and Production: Own the bridge between the Application Development team(s) and the Production Environment.

The listed responsibilities are not exhaustive and additional responsibilities may be assigned based on the evolving needs of the organization. We are seeking a dynamic individual who is able to adapt and take on new responsibilities as they arise.

Clearance & Travel Requirements

  • Clearance Requirement: Active Secret clearance highly preferred.
  • Travel Expectations: 10%–25%.

Required Experience and Qualifications

  • Proven experience as a Platform Engineer or similar role, with a focus on system architecture and development.
  • Demonstrated experience with cloud-native technologies such as Kubernetes, Google Cloud, and Docker.
  • Familiarity with continuous delivery, distributed architectures, systems, everything-as-code, containerization, and cloud services.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Go, Ansible) and a basic understanding of shell scripting.
  • Proficient with YAML.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
  • Comfort with debugging systems and reading/writing code.
  • Knowledgeable about DevSecOps/DevOps and CI/CD theory.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a clearance.

Preferred Experience and Qualifications

  • Active Secret security clearance or higher.
  • Experienced in working on a team following an Agile framework in a remote environment.
  • Experience with security automation and familiarity with API Security, Container Security, and Cloud Security.
  • Familiar with architecture security design, monitoring, and performance instrumentation in a complex enterprise environment.
  • Possess a DoD 8570 IAT II certification.
  • Experienced in Department of Defense work, specifically working on a production Authority to Operate (ATO’d) system.

Who We Are

Defense Unicorns delivers mission value by streamlining software delivery so our customers can focus on the most important challenges. We share a vision of freedom and security for the advancement of progress and innovation. Our commitment to this vision, and to our mission-driven customers, means a commitment to speed, user experience and optionality, without compromising security. Our team is composed of innovators, software engineers, and veterans with decades of experience delivering technology programs across the federal market.

What We Do

We create and deliver secure solutions for continuous software integration and delivery. Defense Unicorns consolidates the best practices for security pipelines, testing, and deployment automation in order to meet the high security requirements valued by mission owners. Our solutions are agnostic by design and we believe that growing a robust ecosystem of secure, cloud-native software solutions can help enterprise customers inside and outside the federal market buy and integrate software more easily.

Who We Serve

Defense Unicorns’ customers are mission-focused leaders across public and private enterprises. We proudly support defense and civil agencies across the U.S. government and we work closely with the creators of leading-edge software solutions to deliver value to the mission-owner by improving the security and consumability of commercial software products.

What We Work On

  • Kubernetes
  • Cloud Environments (AWS/GCP and Azure)
  • Infrastructure-as-code (like Terraform/Pulumi)
  • Continuous Delivery and automation tooling
  • GitOps
  • Containers
  • CNCF projects and open source products and packages
  • Helm/Kustomize-Value Stream Mapping
  • Building and improving security delivery
  • Building Kubernetes and cloud native applications

Benefits Our Unicorns Enjoy

Health:

  • Medical/Dental/Vision
  • Premiums are 100% Company Paid
  • Health Savings Account
  • Life Insurance
  • Disability Insurance

Financial:

  • 401k Retirement Plan
  • Company Stock Options
  • Home Office Budget

Leave:

  • We offer all full-time Unicorns Flexible Time Off (FTO) plus all Federal Holidays, one week for Thanksgiving, and two weeks for Christmas and New Year’s
  • Paid Parental Leave

Learning:

  • Reimbursement for approved trainings/subscriptions
  • Conferences (travel, lodging, and fees)

Don’t have all the preferred experience or qualifications? Studies show that underrepresented groups like women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs if they don't meet every requirement listed.

At Defense Unicorns, we're committed to diversity. If you're enthusiastic about the role but don't match every criteria, we encourage you to apply. You could be the perfect fit for this or another role! Defense Unicorns is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, veteran status, genetic information, union status and/or beliefs, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

  • Own the Kanban process (we use Linear) and drive an adaptable but disciplined sprint process across engineers, designers, UX experts, business leaders and data engineers.
  • Aling with multiple stakeholders on roadmap, near and long-term priorities, and drive deliverables and outcomes via on time delivery.

Product strategy and roadmap

  • Own the GPS multi-quarter roadmap and the reasoning behind it. Maintain a defensible prioritization model that survives executive pressure and aligns with Greystar’s global priorities.
  • Translate operational and investment problems into product scope. Kill work that does not earn its place.
  • Define and defend the boundary between GPS (the product) and DMP (the platform) — what belongs in the product versus the underlying data infrastructure.

Delivery partnership

  • Work daily with the builders and workstream leads across pipeline and orchestration, architecture, permissions and entitlements, infrastructure, and business stakeholder coordination.
  • Own requirements, acceptance criteria, and UAT outcomes. Own the release narrative.
  • Hold the line on quality where data trust is at stake — a wrong number in GPS costs more credibility than a late feature.
  • Run deep with the data and data engineering teams to troubleshoot and understand solutions when data discrepancies arise.

Qualifications

Required

  • 8+ years in product management, with at least 3 years owning enterprise data, analytics, or reporting products used by non-technical business users.
  • You are a product manager, tactical operator and also a builder. You tinker with AI, Openclaw, Cowork or anything else that keeps you building and learning. You push to production.
  • Demonstrated ownership of a product where the primary value was trusted numbers — including responsibility for metric definitions, not just interfaces.
  • Working fluency with modern data platform concepts: lakehouse and medallion patterns, semantic and reporting layers, data lineage, row- and column-level entitlements, pipeline SLAs. You do not need to build them; you need to reason about trade-offs with the people who do.
  • Track record of operating across a large organization without authority over the stakeholders you depend on, including evidence of arbitrating between senior stakeholders with conflicting interests.
  • Ability to write for and present to executive audiences — concise, numbers-first, with the reasoning available on request.

Strongly preferred (but not required for rock stars who don’t have the below experience)

  • Real estate, property management, Financial or PropTech domain experience; familiarity with Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage data models.
  • Experience in a multi-source-system environment where the same concept is represented differently by each system.
  • Experience with global rollout where operational definitions vary by market (US vs. UK/EU vs. APAC).
  • Exposure to data governance and metric certification programs.

  • Payment Processing: Process, apply, and reconcile customer payments and credit memos accurately within Dynamics and Acumatica ERP systems.

  • Reporting: Maintain accurate account records and prepare reporting related to AR aging, account status, collections activity, and critical account updates.
  • Leadership Engagement: Participate in weekly meetings with the CFO and Financial Controller to provide updates on critical accounts, collection risks, and overall AR performance.

Qualifications:

  • Excellent English communication skills, both written and verbal.
  • Strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Previous experience in billing, finance, accounting, collections, customer support, or a similar role is a plus.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with numbers, data, and financial information.

Benefits

  • Partner with Engineering, Fulfillment Operations, and other cross-functional teams to identify opportunities, improve operational workflows, and strengthen the systems supporting lottery fulfillment.
  • Elevate engineering standards through code reviews, technical documentation, automated testing, and mentorship while contributing to the team's broader data infrastructure.


What you’ll bring

  • A Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, with at least 3 years of machine learning engineering experience.
  • Proven experience developing, deploying, and maintaining machine learning models in production environments.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and software engineering best practices, including automated testing, data validation, and asynchronous programming.
  • Hands-on experience with computer vision, multimodal or vision-language models, and machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT, or vLLM.
  • Experience with model fine-tuning, prompt design, performance evaluation, and image processing tools such as OpenCV.
  • Experience with cloud-based machine learning platforms, preferably Google Cloud, and familiarity with containerization, orchestration, and monitoring tools such as Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, or Datadog.
  • Strong technical ownership, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to lead complex initiatives, explain technical decisions, and collaborate across teams.

Position Summary

The Software Developer II designs, builds, tests, and supports enterprise Salesforce solutions on a large enterprise Salesforce platform. These two positions are dedicated to the transition from Salesforce Education Data Architecture (EDA) to Salesforce Education Cloud. The developer works in an Agile delivery environment with frequent production releases. This is a hands-on development position requiring immediate proficiency in Salesforce development and the Salesforce education data model.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain Salesforce applications using Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flows, and custom objects.
  • Build and maintain integrations between Salesforce, external partner data feeds, a learning management system, MuleSoft, and AWS GovCloud services using REST and SOAP APIs, platform events, and middleware.
  • Deliver the Education Cloud migration by analyzing existing customizations, implementing approved configurations, supporting Person Account conversion and data validation, and testing integrations against the new data model.
  • Configure, develop, and test approved Agentforce capabilities, actions, and integrations within established governance and security requirements.
  • Participate in sprint planning, backlog refinement, standups, demonstrations, and retrospectives. Provide accurate development estimates and time reporting against assigned Jira tickets.
  • Deliver well-tested code that meets documented acceptance criteria, passes established quality checks, and minimizes defects introduced into production.
  • Apply secure coding practices and implement assigned controls consistent with applicable federal security, privacy, and Section 508 accessibility requirements. Remediate assigned vulnerabilities within established timelines.
  • Document designs, technical decisions, and configuration changes in Jira and Confluence. Support production incident investigation, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a closely related field.
  • Minimum of four years of professional software development experience.
  • Current hands-on Salesforce development experience using Apex and Lightning Web Components in a production organization within the last 12 months.
  • Hands-on development experience on Salesforce Education Cloud or Education Data Architecture, including the data model.
  • Experience implementing Salesforce integrations using REST APIs, SOAP APIs, platform events, or middleware such as MuleSoft.
  • Experience with Git-based source control, unit testing, debugging, and deployments across development, testing, and production environments.
  • Active Salesforce Trailblazer account with a public profile.
  • U.S. citizenship.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a favorably adjudicated federal background investigation. A security clearance is not required.
  • Ability to handle and safeguard Controlled Unclassified Information.

Required Salesforce Certifications

All certification requirements must be current and verifiable:

  • Salesforce Certified Platform Developer (formerly Platform Developer I).
  • One of: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II, Platform Administrator, or Platform App Builder.
  • Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist.

Candidates must list their certifications on their resumes and provide their Trailblazer profile URL. Required certifications will be verified before interviews are scheduled.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating Salesforce with a learning management system, including data exchange between the two.
  • Salesforce Certified Education Cloud Consultant certification.
  • Experience supporting Salesforce data model migrations, including Person Accounts.
  • Experience with MuleSoft, AWS GovCloud, Experience Cloud, or Tableau.
  • Experience implementing Agentforce solutions in a production environment.
  • Experience supporting federal government technology programs.

jobs.description:
Crimson Education helps ambitious students apply to the world’s top universities. Crimson students have received more than 1,490 Ivy League offers.

This role sits within AdmitYogi, Crimson’s lighter-touch college admissions mentoring program. Students work one-on-one with a current Ivy League student or graduate. Some join us early in high school for long-term mentoring, building a multi-year roadmap and meeting their mentor every two weeks to put it into action. Others join closer to applications for focused support with their college list, essays and applications.

The role

You’ll lead Zoom strategy calls with students and parents who have already booked time with AdmitYogi. You’ll get to know the student, answer the family’s questions about college admissions, and recommend a mentoring or application support package that fits their goals and timeline.

Most families take time to decide, so follow-up is a core part of the job. You’ll set aside time each shift to send tailored proposals, answer questions, and help families make an informed decision. You’ll report directly to Todd Anderson, AdmitYogi’s CEO.

What you’ll do

  • Lead scheduled Zoom calls with students and parents and answer questions about admissions timelines, testing, extracurriculars, and essays.

  • Recommend the right AdmitYogi package for each student and explain what’s included and what it costs. Give families honest advice and avoid promising admissions outcomes.

  • Own the sales process from the first call through enrollment, including following up, closing sales, and meeting sales targets.

  • Send personalized follow-up emails and proposals, keep track of each family’s next step, and guide them through enrollment.

  • Follow up by text and email when families miss a scheduled call.

  • Keep HubSpot up to date and brief the student’s mentor on what you learned once the family enrolls.

Who you are

  • Dependable. Families set aside time to meet with you. You might have 20 calls booked in a week, and you're the type of person who won't miss one, week after week.

  • Proactive. You follow through on what you promise, keep your pipeline organized, and know when to reach out again.

  • Quick to learn. We’ll train you on AdmitYogi’s programs and sales process. You’ll be expected to build enough admissions knowledge to answer families’ questions confidently.

  • Warm, curious, and honest. You enjoy speaking with parents and teenagers, ask thoughtful questions, and give families room to decide.

Experience in sales, admissions counseling, tutoring, or another client-facing role is a plus. So is firsthand experience with the US college admissions process or familiarity with a CRM such as HubSpot.

Hours and pay

  • Hours: 15–25 hours per week. You’ll work at least three evenings a week, ideally four or five.

  • Schedule: 4:30–9:30 p.m. Eastern Time on your scheduled evenings, including paid time for follow-up.

  • Pay: US$20 per hour plus 5% commission on payments received from families you enroll. Commission is paid monthly and includes future installments as they’re collected.

  • Typical earnings: around US$35–45 per hour all-in, growing the longer you’re with us.

  • Location: Fully remote within the US.

  • Start dates: December 2026 for the first hire, with additional hires starting in mid-January 2027.

If you enjoy talking with students and parents and helping families make informed decisions about college admissions support, we’d love to hear from you.

To apply, submit your résumé, tell us which evenings you can consistently work, and record a ~90 second response to a sample family call.

After you apply, please check your spam or junk folder for updates from Teamtailor.

jobs.description:
Role summary

The Project Manager III plans and coordinates all aspects of large-scale Data Center network builds and retrofits from initiation to delivery, including AI implementations. Working with project coordinators, deployment engineers, data center technicians, site teams, program partners, logistics providers, and internal customers, the PM III turns approved intake and roadmap requirements into clear execution plans. This role defines project requirements, conducts feasibility and needs/impact assessments, and manages all implementation processes including asset management, resource allocation, progress tracking, change control monitoring, documentation, training, and on-time delivery within budget constraints across projects of varying number, size, and complexity.


The successful candidate understands the purpose of the work, connects technical and material dependencies to the schedule, identifies what is preventing progress, and brings the right people together to resolve it. After structured onboarding, the PM III is expected to lead familiar deployment scopes independently within established decision rights, while seeking engineering clarification for new or ambiguous technical scope.


The assigned portfolio may span multiple sites and include new-build network deployments, retrofits, platform changes, capacity additions, migrations and selected non-repeatable initiatives.


Key responsibilities

Project intake, planning and kickoff

  • Partner with functional teams during initiation, planning, design, procurement, deployment, and post-deployment phases; participate in defining project scope and objectives involving all relevant stakeholders to ensure technical feasibility.
  • Review engineering deployment plans and the bill of materials (BOM) with the deployment engineer; confirm delivery locations, site readiness, dependencies, and discrepancies before committing detailed execution plans.
  • Coordinate the appropriate deployment engineer, site execution partners and logistics support with their responsible leads; document who owns each activity.
  • Create or coordinate the appropriate workstreams and role assignments using the approved process.
  • Schedule and lead focused kickoff discussions and regularly scheduled meetings with core teams to establish scope, responsibilities, milestones, material need-by dates, risks, and next actions.

Portfolio and delivery ownership

  • Maintain the assigned site/region roadmap and project trackers, incorporating inputs and tracking program milestones, timelines, and overall deliverables for multiple cross-functional network deployment projects.
  • Coordinate interdependent engineering, field, material and site-readiness activities. Identify the critical blockers, responsible owners, recovery actions and expected resolution dates.
  • Lead recurring delivery reviews, measure project performance using metrics and KPIs via appropriate tools, and maintain steady updates without unnecessary duplicate meetings.
  • Keep schedule dates, roles, comments, and status accurate; monitor change control processes, date comments, preserve approved baselines, and advocate proper change management.
  • Reconcile portfolio coverage, supported work and handover records so transferred ownership, incomplete tags or engineer-owned work do not disappear from delivery visibility.

Materials and field coordination

  • Responsible for asset and material management across data centers and warehouses, partnering with the PC on BOM completeness, inbound material availability, need-by dates, site receiving readiness, and delivery sequencing.
  • Ensure material plans support the actual deployment sequence, including phased suite or megapod delivery where applicable.
  • Provide direction and resolve or escalate discrepancies affecting the schedule while the PC performs the assigned tactical tracking and material-request activities.
  • Coordinate with technical and field owners on installation, validation and readiness evidence; do not substitute an administrative update for an engineering deliverable.

Stakeholder communication, risk and closeout

  • Own clear communication for assigned projects; act as a main point of contact for vendor partners, internal stakeholders, and client executives, providing regular status updates, risk analysis, and progress metrics.
  • Identify and track risks, execute risk analysis and management techniques, and present feasible risk mitigation strategies when priorities, site capacity, material availability, or network restrictions conflict.
  • Engage in creating and maintaining comprehensive project documentation including schedules, reviews, process documents, and risk analysis; drive lifecycle milestones from concept commit through project closure.
  • Follow approved closeout and exception procedures.
  • Participate in portfolio and workload planning.

Continuity and continuous improvement

  • Prepare usable handovers covering scope, contacts, current dates, materials, open actions, risks, evidence and outstanding decisions.
  • Contribute practical examples, process documentation and lessons learned to the team's onboarding library and operating playbooks.
  • Support peer learning and mentoring within an agreed capacity plan; raise training or access gaps before they affect delivery.
  • Participate in internal process improvements to eliminate gaps across multiple teams/functions; evaluate post-project results against metrics to recommend or implement improvements to delivery processes.

Required qualifications — proposed for this draft

  • Bachelor’s degree (B.S./B.A.) with 2–5 years of related project management experience in a fast-paced environment supporting data centers, network hardware, or large-scale network lifecycles (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
  • Proven ability to manage multiple, cross-functional technical projects concurrently, translating scope into detailed project plans, resource allocations, risk analysis, and tracking metrics.
  • Understanding of data center lifecycles, large-scale network deployment activities (equipment installation, rack/stack/cabling, site readiness, validation), and asset management across data centers and warehouses.
  • Strong track record of building productive internal and external working relationships with vendors, field teams, logistics partners, and client executives, exercising sound judgment within defined procedures to resolve conflicts and meet schedule timelines.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and documentation skills, including experience creating spreadsheets, presentation materials, meeting summaries, and process documentation.
  • Self-starter who can quickly learn new tools, processes, and technologies with minimal assistance, and work flexibly across multiple North American timezones (remotely or locally).
  • Ability to distinguish delivery progress, missing evidence and administrative closure, and maintain accurate records when stakeholders are pressing for completion.
  • Strong observational and analytical skills with high attention to detail, accuracy, risk mitigation, and metric tracking.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in hyperscale data centers, network infrastructure deployment or a managed-service delivery environment.
  • Experience with both new-build and retrofit/migration work, or with Optical terminal/transponder and capacity-add delivery interfaces.

jobs.description:
Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

We’re looking for a detail-oriented and organized Remote Bookkeeper to support the finance team with day-to-day accounting and administrative tasks for a property management portfolio.

In this role, you’ll work primarily with AppFolio and QuickBooks Online to manage accounts payable and receivable, process payments, reconcile bank and trust accounts, maintain accurate financial records, and support month-end reporting.

You’ll handle a high volume of daily transactions and work closely with the Director of Finance, while communicating with vendors, tenants, property owners, and internal team members. The ideal candidate has bookkeeping experience, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage financial tasks independently in a remote environment.

What You’ll Own

Accounts Payable

  • Review, code, and enter vendor invoices in AppFolio.
  • Create in-house maintenance invoices and bill tenants for tenant-caused repairs.
  • Follow up on past-due invoices and respond to vendor payment inquiries.
  • Maintain accurate vendor records, including W-9s, insurance documents, and payment methods.
  • Prepare 1099 forms.

Accounts Receivable & Tenant Ledgers

  • Post and reconcile rent receipts, deposits, and chargebacks.
  • Prepare move-out security deposit dispositions within required timelines.
  • Track overdue tenant payments and follow established collection policies.
  • Maintain accurate collections logs and tenant account records.

Bank & Trust Reconciliations

  • Reconcile operating, rent trust, and security deposit trust accounts daily.
  • Investigate and resolve outstanding items, non-sufficient funds (NSF) transactions, and unmatched payments.
  • Ensure financial transactions are accurately recorded and reconciled.

Month-End & Administrative Support

  • Generate month-end reports and gather supporting documentation for the Director of Finance.
  • Process owner distributions once approved.
  • Monitor the finance inbox and respond to or route inquiries from owners, tenants, and staff.
  • Keep owner, tenant, and vendor contact and payment information up to date.

Company Bookkeeping – QuickBooks Online

  • Record receipts and expenses for company entities.
  • Review and accurately categorize financial transactions.
  • Prepare weekly billable-hours reports.
  • Support commission and payroll data preparation.

Required Experience & Skills

  • At least 2 years of experience in bookkeeping or accounting support, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and bank reconciliations.
  • Proficiency in AppFolio and QuickBooks Online.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets.
  • Strong data entry skills with excellent accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage a high volume of daily transactions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for working with owners, tenants, vendors, and internal teams.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment and follow established procedures.
  • High level of professionalism and commitment to confidentiality when handling financial information.

Nice to Have

  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • Experience in property management accounting.
  • Familiarity with tenant ledgers, owner distributions, and security deposit accounting.
  • Experience maintaining vendor records and preparing 1099 forms.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You are highly organized and comfortable handling detailed, repetitive financial tasks.
  • You can manage multiple accounting priorities while maintaining accuracy.
  • You take ownership of daily responsibilities and follow established processes.
  • You proactively investigate discrepancies and follow up on unresolved transactions.
  • You communicate professionally and handle sensitive financial information with discretion.
  • You are reliable, self-motivated, and comfortable working independently in a remote setting.

What Success Looks Like

  • Vendor invoices, payments, and tenant transactions are processed accurately and on time.
  • Bank and trust accounts are reconciled daily, with discrepancies investigated promptly.
  • Tenant ledgers, vendor records, and financial information remain accurate and up to date.
  • Month-end reports and supporting documents are prepared reliably.
  • Owner distributions and other financial tasks are completed according to approval procedures.
  • The Director of Finance receives consistent and dependable bookkeeping support.

Interview Process

  • Initial Screening
  • Recruiter Interview
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Onboarding

Job Summary

The Tax Manager is responsible for managing the Company's federal, state, and local tax compliance obligations, covering income/franchise and indirect taxes across a multi-state footprint of approximately 45 states and various local jurisdictions.

The Tax Manager coordinates compliance activities with internal teams and external tax advisors. The role reviews the work of the Senior Tax Accountant and helps build scalable tax processes.

The ideal candidate will have a minimum of 5-7 years of progressive corporate tax experience in direct as well as indirect taxes.

Essential Functions

Compliance Oversight and External Liaison

  • Manage the corporate tax compliance calendar, ensuring all deadlines for federal, state, and local tax returns (income, franchise, gross receipts, sales/use) are met on time and accurately.
  • Review tax returns and extensions, along with supporting workpapers, including state apportionment and federal-to-state tax modifications.
  • Manage the documentation and timely remittance of estimated federal and state tax payments.
  • Liaise with internal teams and external advisors.
  • Coordinate international tax compliance including data compilation and review.

Tax Notices and Taxing Authority Correspondence

  • Own the end-to-end tax notice process for federal, state, and local jurisdictions, including receiving notices, logging, research, response, and resolution tracking.
  • Analyze notices (balance due, penalty, assessment, information requests) and submit well-supported responses.
  • Communicate directly with state and local taxing authorities to resolve account discrepancies and close out open matters.

Team Leadership, Tax Research and Strategy

  • Review the Senior Tax Accountant’s work and provide guidance, training, and feedback.
  • Stay current with federal, state, and local tax legislative changes that could impact the Company's tax obligations.
  • Identify potential tax-saving opportunities.

Sales & Use Tax and Other Indirect Taxes

  • Partner with Project Management teams to review new projects and contracts for potential sales, use, and gross receipts tax implications, ensuring proper customer billing and collection of applicable indirect taxes.
  • Review and oversee resale/exemption certificate management.

Information Requests and Tax Records

  • Own information requests from external advisors and compile the requested information.
  • Maintain audit-ready tax workpapers and documentation.
  • Organize and archive tax-related data and records.

State Registrations and Annual Reports

  • Manage state and local tax registrations (sales and use, income/franchise, gross receipts, withholding coordination, and business licenses).
  • Maintain registrations inventory covering account numbers, filing frequencies, and portal access.
  • Handle account updates, filing frequency changes, closures, and responses to registration-related correspondence.

  • In-depth knowledge of C-Corporation federal income tax compliance and multi-state corporate income/franchise tax laws.
  • Proficiency with indirect tax (sales and use, gross receipts) related to the services sector.
  • Demonstrated experience independently resolving tax notices and overseeing state registrations.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple concurrent deadlines across 45+ jurisdictions.

jobs.excerpt: Company overview Orbiss is an advisory and tax firm specialized in business growth in the United States.
jobs.description:
Company overview

Orbiss is an advisory and tax firm specialized in business growth in the United States. Founded in 2020, Orbiss helps international small and medium-sized private companies successfully scale up in the United States.

The firm offers a 360° and tailor-made support to its clients' cross-border accounting, tax, and M&A transaction needs. The Orbiss team’s vision is modernity. This vision is implemented through an innovative approach focusing on processes automation and aiming to place people at the heart of every decision, every day, in line with our values: kindness, honesty, respect, and integrity.

Orbiss is an innovative, modern, and young firm breaking old habits of the industry.

As a Tax Manager, you will be responsible for:

Position Summary:

The Tax Manager leads a portfolio of corporate and partnership clients and a team of 3–6 collaborators. The role combines final review of returns, people leadership, and a trusted advisory relationship with clients, while shaping, alongside Senior Management, how our Corporate Tax practice grows: its quality standards, its processes, and the tools that make it modern.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Owning a portfolio of corporate and partnership clients: Act as the main point of contact for your clients, ensure every deadline is met, and make sure every filing reflects the Firm's standards of quality and accuracy.
  • Leading accounts across a range of industries and revenue sizes: Guide clients from $0 to $100M in sectors such as Tech Start-Ups, Pharmaceuticals, Marketing, Consumer Products, and our personal favorite, French Wine and Desserts.
  • Performing the final quality review: Review and sign off on returns prepared by Associates, Seniors and Senior Leads, acting as the final quality check before submission.
  • Planning and managing team engagements: Plan, schedule and staff your team’s engagements across a team of 3–6, in person and remote. Balance workloads, flag over- or under-utilization to management, and review and approve timesheets.
  • Coaching and developing your people: Provide on-the-job training and regular performance feedback, support each collaborator’s growth path, and take part in performance reviews and promotions.
  • Sharing knowledge and driving continuous learning: Use technology to keep learning, share knowledge and tax updates with the team, maintain a training program to develop skills, and drive automation to enhance service delivery.
  • Handling complex engagements and technical guidance: Lead consolidations, multistate filings, nexus and apportionment, entity structuring, and international compliance forms (5472, 5471, 8865, 8858, 1042-S, and FinCEN 114).
  • Acting as a strategic partner to clients: Keep clients fully informed of engagement progress, participate actively in client meetings and in business and tax planning efforts, and turn tax questions into growth opportunities.
  • Collaborating across the Firm: Maintain cooperative relationships with other engagement teams (Accounting, Consulting, Private Clients, Payroll) and contribute, with Senior Management, to the Corporate Tax strategy and quality group.
  • Embodying the Orbiss culture: Promote the Firm's mission and values (respect, honesty, integrity and kindness) and lead by example in team initiatives and company culture events.

Requirements

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field (Master’s degree in Taxation is a plus).
  • CPA license, or actively working toward it.

Experience:

  • 5+ years of experience in US corporate and partnership taxation within a public accounting or tax advisory firm.
  • 3+ years of experience managing, coaching and reviewing the work of tax staff.
  • Proven experience managing multiple client accounts and engagements concurrently, including international compliance forms and cross-border matters.

Technical Skills:

  • Advanced knowledge of US federal and state corporate and partnership taxation, including consolidations and multistate matters.
  • Proficiency in tax preparation software, Microsoft Excel, and workflow and automation tools.

Soft Skills:

  • Leadership: You plan, delegate, and grow your team with clear, constructive and kind feedback.
  • Client Partnership: You explain complex tax matters clearly, communicate proactively, and push back when needed.
  • Trust & Discretion: You handle sensitive client information with integrity, confidentiality, and reliability.
  • Ownership: You respect deadlines and flag early when things shift.
  • Organization: You manage multiple clients, reviews, and team priorities efficiently and calmly.

Fluency in both English and French is a plus (written and spoken). US work authorization required.

Benefits

Did we mention Orbiss’s benefits?

  • 🏥 Health insurance 100% covered, with HSA & FSA options
  • 💰 401(k) with 100% match up to 6% — starting after 3 months
  • 🌴 Unlimited PTO (with a real minimum of 2 weeks — we mean it)

  • Our shared values that foster inclusion and belonging including uncompromising integrity, collaboration, trust, and mutual respect

  • The opportunity to innovate and do work that motivates and engages you

  • A collaborative environment focused on enabling you to further your career growth and continuous professional development

  • Competitive compensation and a total rewards package that focuses on all aspects of your wellbeing

jobs.title: Linux Patching Engineer
jobs.excerpt: What success looks like in this role: Position Summary The Linux Patching Engineer is responsible for patching activities across enterprise Linux environments, particularly Red Hat Enterprise Linux, including planning, testing, scheduling, deployment, validation, compliance reporting, exception management, and remediation.
jobs.description:
What success looks like in this role:

Position Summary


The Linux Patching Engineer is responsible for patching activities across enterprise Linux environments, particularly Red Hat Enterprise Linux, including planning, testing, scheduling, deployment, validation, compliance reporting, exception management, and remediation.


The engineer ensures operating system, kernel, and core package patches are deployed consistently, safely, and in line with security, operational, and customer requirements, improving audit readiness and reducing exposure to known vulnerabilities.


The engineer works with the Linux Vulnerability Engineer to prioritize patching based on risk and customer requirements, and with the Patching Automation Engineer to automate what can be automated. The role also partners with Linux and Unix administrators, application owners, change management, service delivery, and the Windows and Middleware Patching Engineers. The Linux Patching Engineer owns patch execution and outcomes; the Patching Automation Engineer builds and maintains reusable automation.


Key Responsibilities

  • Own and perform patching activities across on-premises and cloud Linux servers, including kernel updates, core packages (glibc, OpenSSL, OpenSSH), vendor errata, and minor release updates.
  • Track Red Hat Security Advisories and vendor errata; with the Linux Vulnerability Engineer, prioritize patches by severity, exploitability, system criticality, operational risk, and customer requirements; and maintain routine and emergency schedules aligned with SLAs and maintenance requirements.
  • Manage patch content in Red Hat Satellite or an equivalent platform (content views, lifecycle environments, repository snapshots) to give each environment a tested, consistent baseline.
  • Review errata, dependencies, and known issues; coordinate testing across development, test, staging, disaster recovery, and production, accounting for application compatibility, third-party agents and kernel modules, and high-availability clusters such as Pacemaker.
  • Prepare implementation, validation, communication, and backout plans; maintain change records (risk assessments, approvals, test evidence, affected systems); and confirm backup and recovery readiness before deployment.
  • Lead patch readiness and go/no-go reviews; coordinate deployments and reboot sequencing in approved windows, apply kernel live patches where supported, and verify systems, applications, services, and clusters afterward.
  • Troubleshoot package conflicts, repository errors, failed kernel updates, and post-patch boot or service issues; coordinate rollback or recovery, escalate service-impacting failures, and apply lessons learned to future cycles.
  • Work with the Linux Vulnerability Engineer to turn vulnerability findings into patching plans; reconcile scanner results, Satellite errata status, deployment records, and asset inventories to close coverage gaps and drive failed, overdue, or noncompliant systems to closure.
  • Manage patch exceptions, including end-of-life or extended-support systems; document compensating controls and remediation plans, and retain approval, testing, deployment, and remediation evidence for audits.
  • Work with the Patching Automation Engineer to automate what can be automated, defining, testing, and validating Linux patching workflows (Ansible playbooks, Satellite remote execution jobs, controls, exception handling, recovery) while retaining ownership of execution, compliance, and remediation outcomes.
  • Maintain patch calendars, runbooks, inventories, and dashboards; report compliance, deployment status, failures, exceptions, aging vulnerabilities, and risks; and coordinate shared maintenance windows with the Windows and Middleware Patching Engineers.

You will be successful in this role if you have:

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent education and experience.
  • Six or more years of experience in Linux systems administration, infrastructure operations, patch management, or vulnerability remediation.
  • Hands-on experience patching enterprise Linux servers (physical, virtual, and cloud), including production, clustered, highly available, and disaster recovery environments.
  • Strong working knowledge of Red Hat Enterprise Linux, including DNF/YUM, RPM, repository management, kernel updates, and systemd.
  • Experience planning, testing, deploying, validating, and troubleshooting Linux operating system and kernel patches.
  • Hands-on experience with Red Hat Satellite or an equivalent enterprise Linux patching platform.
  • Working knowledge of Bash, Python, and Ansible for scripting, troubleshooting, and validation.
  • Experience producing patch compliance reports, metrics, and audit evidence; strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills.
  • Ability to support planned maintenance windows and emergency patching outside normal business hours.
  • U.S. Citizenship and U.S. residency required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience administering Red Hat Satellite at enterprise scale, including content views, lifecycle environments, errata management, and remote execution.
  • Experience with kernel live patching (kpatch, Oracle Ksplice), Oracle Linux, and other enterprise Linux distributions.
  • Experience with Ansible Automation Platform, GitLab CI/CD, Terraform, HashiCorp Vault, JFrog Artifactory, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.
  • Experience with Power BI or ServiceNow dashboards.
  • Familiarity with NIST guidance, CIS controls, Red Hat Enterprise Linux STIGs, or comparable security frameworks.
  • Familiarity with Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes, including patching container hosts.
  • Experience leading patching across multiple customers, business units, or distributed environments.

This role may require access to export-controlled commodities and technology. Therefore, to conform to U.S. export control regulations, applicant should be eligible for any required authorizations from the U.S. Government.

jobs.description:
About Enlighten

At Enlighten, we believe AI should expand what people can take on. We build teams of AI agents alongside Fortune 500 companies so they can put their best thinking to work across the business. We want the people closest to the work to be able to ask hard questions and get answers they can trust. Our mission is to give every team the intelligence it needs to make decisions that shape the business.

About the role

You’ll help customers put Enlighten to work after the sale and see whether it’s making the difference they expected. You’ll own the ongoing relationship, from onboarding through adoption and renewal preparation.

What you'll do

  • Lead onboarding and regular customer conversations. Agree on goals, milestones, owners, and next steps.
  • Learn how each customer’s teams work, what decisions they’re trying to improve, and which data or workflow issues are getting in their way.
  • Review usage and customer feedback to show what teams have adopted, what outcomes the evidence supports, and where they need help.
  • Run multiple AI agents in parallel every day to prepare account briefs, summarize feedback, and draft follow-ups. Check the work before sharing it with customers.
  • Build small tools with agents to organize customer context, track follow-ups, and prepare account health reviews.
  • Coordinate product, delivery, solutions, and commercial teams around open questions and risks. Start expansion or renewal planning early with evidence and clear next decisions.
  • Share recurring customer feedback with the teams that can improve the product, enablement, or delivery.

What you bring

  • Experience in customer success, account management, consulting, implementation, or another role supporting customers after a sale or project start.
  • A calm, direct communication style that can build trust while addressing ambiguity, risk, or unmet expectations early.
  • Strong organization and follow-through across multiple customer relationships and internal contributors.
  • Practical AI fluency. You can run multiple agents for research, drafting, checking, and coordination, then validate the output and own the customer conversation.
  • Comfort building small custom apps or workflows with agent assistance to improve preparation, tracking, and customer context.
  • The initiative to spot a missing decision, unclear owner, or emerging risk and move it toward resolution without waiting for detailed direction.
  • Good judgment about customer confidentiality, product limits, and the difference between a goal, an activity, and a verified outcome.
  • Experience with enterprise analytics, data, measurement, or AI-enabled products; coordinating renewals with account executives or commercial leaders; and creating customer-health or outcome-review workflows.
  • You work independently. You can take an unclear goal, decide what to do first, find what you need, and carry the work through to a result. You bring people in early when a decision, risk, or dependency needs their input.

How we work

AI agents are core to how we get work done. You'll spend a substantial part of your day running multiple agents in parallel, building tools and workflows with them, and checking what they produce. You own the result. Verify the facts, calculations, code, and claims before they go into a decision, a customer conversation, or a release.

When working with clients, take initiative within the agreed goals, scope, access permissions, and review process. Bring options and recommendations, and involve the right people before changing a customer commitment or production workflow.

What success looks like

  • Customers have clear goals, active owners, and a reliable rhythm for addressing questions and decisions.
  • Adoption and outcome conversations are evidence-based, candid, and useful to the customer.
  • Renewal conversations start early, with clear context and known risks already surfaced.

Position Summary

The Consortium for Brain Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN) is an academic-industry consortium directed by Dr. Randall J. Bateman, Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. C-BRAIN brings together academic research institutions, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, technology partners, philanthropic organizations, and government agencies to develop AI-powered tools to accelerate discovery in Alzheimer's disease and neurodegenerative disorders. Washington University serves as the coordinating center for C-BRAIN. C-BRAIN is currently deploying initial versions of the tools and developing plans for benchmarking and evaluation of the tools in addition to platform integration and scaling. C-BRAIN is also working on development of foundational AI models for brain aging and neurodegeneration. See www.c-brain.org.

The C-BRAIN Senior Applied Scientist, Foundation Models, leads the design, training, and evaluation of C-BRAIN's biological foundation models for brain aging and neurodegeneration. Reporting to the C-BRAIN Chief Technology Officer (CTO), with scientific direction from C-BRAIN scientific leadership, this role turns large spatial biology, brain imaging, and longitudinal clinical trial datasets into models that researchers can use through C-BRAIN's AI tools. The work spans self-supervised model design for spatial multi-omic data, controlled scaling studies from hundreds of millions toward billions of parameters, privacy-preserving training in which each data contributor's data trains its own expert model, and the path from trained model to production. The first models to reach researchers are small expert models trained on each contributor's clinical trial, registry, and biomarker data; foundation models on spatial and imaging data follow.
The ideal candidate has built and trained large self-supervised models on spatial biology and other scientific data, designs experiments that show whether scale actually helps, and works well with other scientists, data engineers, leadership, and software engineers.

Job Description

Primary Duties & Responsibilities:

Foundation Model Research and Development

  • Lead the design of foundation models for spatial multi-omic brain data: encoders that handle different measurement panels across datasets, spatial and cross-scale context from subcellular to regional levels, and fusion of transcriptomic, genomic, proteomic, and imaging longitudinal measurements.
  • Define and implement self-supervised training objectives (for example, masked measurement prediction, spatial-neighbor prediction, and cross-scale prediction), and determine which data modalities add the most information.
  • Extend models to brain imaging and longitudinal clinical and biomarker data, and design how independently trained expert models combine into an assembly of experts.
  • Prepare training-ready datasets with C-BRAIN data engineers: quality control, batch-effect assessment, harmonization across sites and platforms, and train, validation, and held-out splits that prevent leakage.
  • Track the research field and adapt published methods and open models where they fit.

Scaling Studies and Training Infrastructure

  • Design and run controlled scaling studies across data volume, compute, and model size; fit scaling curves; and recommend when larger models are justified.
  • Train models from tens of millions toward billions of parameters on multi-node GPU clusters using distributed training (for example, PyTorch FSDP, DeepSpeed, or Megatron-Core) and schedulers such as Slurm.
  • Build efficient data pipelines for very large imaging and spatial datasets, and measure GPU utilization, throughput, and cost so results reflect the model rather than infrastructure bottlenecks.
  • Maintain reproducible training: versioned data and code, experiment tracking, checkpoints, and documented configurations.

Evaluation and Biological Validation

  • Build benchmarks and evaluation suites with domain scientists: embedding geometry analyses, recovery of known biological relationships, and downstream tasks such as cell-type identification, disease staging, and brain-age prediction.
  • Compare models against published baselines and simpler methods, and report results with uncertainty and clear limitations.
  • Probe learned representations for new biological structure and work with scientists to test the resulting hypotheses.

Privacy-Preserving and Expert-Partitioned Training

  • Train on contributed consortium data only through the privacy-preserving methods consortium data agreements require: per-contributor expert partitions, federated or confidential computation, and privacy protections applied to model parameters before they leave a protected environment.
  • Evaluate privacy risk in trained models (for example, membership inference and data reconstruction) and apply mitigations such as differential privacy where needed.
  • Work with C-BRAIN engineers and the partner-managed data and model-training platform on secure training environments, access approvals, and model release.

Model-to-Production Integration

  • Package trained models for serving: optimization (for example, distillation and quantization), model cards, versioning, and evaluation gates before release.
  • Work with C-BRAIN software engineers to expose models as tools that AI agents and researchers can call, with provenance on every result.
  • Contribute to production inference code, including Rust-based serving where it improves performance or safety.

Technical Leadership and Scientific Communication

  • Serve as technical lead for C-BRAIN modeling work: guide data scientists, data engineers, and research collaborators through design reviews, code review, and mentoring.
  • Contribute to progress reports, Steering Committee materials, and grant reporting; publish and present results in line with consortium review procedures.
  • Communicate model capabilities and limits clearly to scientists, partners, and non-technical leaders.

Working Conditions:

  • Remote within the United States, per current Washington University policies.
  • Occasional on-site presence required for team meetings and consortium events.
  • Occasional domestic travel may be required for consortium events, partner meetings, or scientific conferences.
  • Standard office environment.
  • Primarily sedentary with standard computer use.

More About This Job

Required Qualifications

  • PhD in machine learning, computer science, computational biology, statistics, or a related field, or a master's degree plus substantial equivalent research or industry experience training large models.
  • Three years of experience after the PhD (or 6 years after a master's degree) building machine learning models on large datasets.

About the role.


PURE is seeking a Senior Platform Engineer to help take our internal developer platform from a strong delivery foundation to a production-grade operating platform. We are in a hardening phase prior to production launch, with meaningful opportunities to shape and build the capabilities that come next. You’ll report to, and work closely with, the AVP of Platform Engineering to build and evolve the product our teams build on. You'll treat the platform as a product: its users are engineers, its interface is a contract they build against, and its success is measured by how much they can do without us. Platform Engineering sits within PURE’s AI Engineering group, but this isn’t an AI role: dedicated AI engineers build the applications, and you’ll build the platform that they, and teams across IDEAS, run on.


The platform’s build-and-release foundation is substantially in place: declarative service registration, versioned Terraform modules, and PR-gated promotion of immutable artifacts across four environments. We run on ECS today, a deliberate choice that keeps our time on platform capabilities rather than cluster operations.


The next chapter is making it production-grade and enabling additional self-service. This is a hands-on execution role that values quality over speed: we build reliability in up front rather than relying on heroics later. You’ll own meaningful work early on, with decision-making scope that grows over time, and your contributions will help define a platform that is still taking shape.


What you'll do.


  • Own the platform’s HCP Terraform Stacks and modules end to end, shipping versioned, backward-compatible releases so consuming teams can adopt new capabilities without disrupting what they already run.
  • Build and extend the reusable GitHub Actions workflows that take every service from commit to production, keeping promotion across environments safe and consistent.
  • Own the platform’s observability and reliability, recommend and implement the tools, standards, and practices that make reliability a property of the platform, so problems are caught early and rarely reach the teams who depend on it.
  • Build the self-service experience: golden paths, automated onboarding, and the documentation that lets a new team ship.
  • Work directly with teams onboarding to the platform, treating their feedback as product input and turning recurring friction into platform features.
  • Own the quality gates every service inherits, building tests, scans, and policies into the platform so the right way is the default.
  • Contribute to how the platform’s compute layer, language support, and shared libraries evolve, evaluating options and bringing recommendations as the services and teams on it diversify.
  • Make the platform measurable, from delivery performance through DORA to cost by service and business area, so the team can see where to invest next.

What you'll need.


We are looking for a hands-on platform engineer who has built and operated production infrastructure, not just provisioned it. You care as much about what happens after a deploy as before it, and you find satisfaction in making the right way the easy way for the teams you support. If a narrowly scoped role would bore you, this one won’t. The ideal candidate will bring:


  • 3-5+ years of experience in Platform Engineering or DevOps.
  • You've built or maintained something other engineers consume as a product, such as a module, library, workflow, or internal tool, and owned its interface: versioning, backward compatibility, documentation, and adoption.
  • Strong AWS proficiency at implementation depth with ECS/Fargate, ALB, and IAM, and working knowledge of the supporting services the platform depends on (CloudWatch, EventBridge, ECR, S3, Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store, Route 53, ACM).
  • Terraform: you’ve written and maintained reusable modules, not just consumed them. Experience with HCP Terraform or Terraform Cloud is a plus, and with HCP Terraform Stacks especially so.
  • GitHub Actions: you’ve built or maintained reusable CI/CD workflows.
  • Scripting skills in Python and/or Bash.
  • Experience with GitOps-style delivery across multiple environments: PR-gated deploys, immutable artifacts, and automated promotion pipelines.
  • Hands-on experience designing observability (metrics, logging, tracing, and alerting) is a plus.
  • Kubernetes experience is welcome but not required; our platform runs on ECS.
  • Familiarity with ML or LLM infrastructure (for example, MLflow, model registries, AI gateways) is a plus.
  • Experience in insurance or financial services is a plus.

Why join PURE.


  • Be the first hire on a platform team that is genuinely building something new, with a working foundation already in place and real influence over what comes next.
  • Work on infrastructure that matters: the platform underpins data, analytics, and ML/AI services that teams across PURE rely on, and every capability you build is inherited by every service on it.
  • Work on hard problems with room to explore, experiment, and build, guided by a high quality bar rather than unnecessary process.
  • Operate in a culture that takes curiosity, collaboration, and craftsmanship seriously, and that measures platform success by the velocity and stability it gives the teams who use it.
  • Join a well-funded, growing IDEAS organization, working alongside colleagues driven by excellence and building the relationships and trust that great engineering depends on.
  • This is a remote position. The team tries to meet in person approximately 1-2 times per year for department on-sites (typically 3–4 days per trip, including travel), with optional opportunities to attend relevant industry or technology conferences.

‌

What We Do

We're a member-owned property and casualty insurer designed exclusively for financially successful families and driven by a purpose of doing what is right for our members. We provide exceptional service, hospitality and care, we partner with our members to help prevent losses and we create smart insurance solutions at fair prices.

We aim for our members to love their insurance. It is our mission is to create a membership experience so compelling that ​our members never want to leave.

Who We Are

We want to be transparent about what we expect from each other. From PURE, you can expect:


Opportunities to stretch and grow: your professional and personal development matters to us. We’re committed to providing experiences through on-the-job learning and professional development that increase your impact and rewards.


Clarity and kindness: you can rely on us to be open, honest and supportive, offering clarity on what success looks like.


Support in good times and bad: we believe in showing up for each other consistently, not only when it’s easy. You can expect a thoughtful partner, even when we disagree.


A community that cares: we are committed to sustaining a community in which each person feels cared for as an individual. We lift each other up, celebrate wins together and support one another through challenges in work and life.

Who You Are

All of the strongest relationships are a partnership- a two way street. So here’s what we ask of you:

  • Aim to bring your best every day: you’re here because you want to be part of a team that makes a real impact and aims high.
  • Be a student and a teacher: share your knowledge and talents and be willing to listen and learn from those around you.
  • Get comfortable being uncomfortable: we face tough moments and obstacles with a “courage over comfort” approach and a positive, solutions-oriented mindset.
  • Be a culture builder: building a positive culture is everyone's responsibility, based on care, respect and openness to diverse perspectives.

‌

The base salary for this role can range from $145,000 to $175,000 based on a full-time work schedule. An individual’s ultimate compensation will vary depending on job-related skills and experience, geographic location, alignment with market data, and equity among other team members with comparable experience.

‌

To ensure a successful onboarding experience, all new hires must work onsite at one of our offices during their first week of employment. Candidates should apply only if they are able to meet this requirement.

jobs.description:
Solvd US

Our organization is redefining claims management across the auto and property space through a blend of AI innovation, proprietary technology, and expert-led services that deliver measurable results for insurers, fleets, rental, TPAs/MGAs, and adjacent industries. Our US team combines automation, intelligence, and human expertise to simplify complex processes — accelerating cycle times, reducing costs, and improving outcomes across appraisal, repair, subrogation response, and auto/property estimating. Our solutions help customers move beyond digital claims to a model that’s faster, smarter, and simpler — grounded in data accuracy, transparency, and customer experience.

As part of the Solvd Group, operating in 46+ countries, our mission is to drive results today while shaping the future of claims. From FNOL to final settlement, we connect technology and expertise to deliver precision, performance, and confidence at every stage.

Position Overview

You will review claim files from first notice of loss (FNOL) through settlement and recovery, recognize great work, and coach adjusters to be even better. Your insights will shape how we handle claims, and you will see the impact of your work across the whole team.

Applicants within a commutable distance to Lenexa, Kansas are preferred, though remote candidates will be considered. At this time, we are offering employment in the following states: AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, FL, GA, IL, IN, KS, LA, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, MT, NV, NJ, NY state, NC, OH, OK, PA, SC, TN, TX, VA, WA, WI.

Key Responsibilities

  • Audit a sample of auto and fleet claim files across the lifecycle (FNOL, coverage check, liability, reserving, repair or total loss, settlement, recovery, closure) against internal standards, client SLAs and state unfair claims settlement practices requirements.
  • Score files and adjusters using the QA scorecard, rating accuracy, timeliness, documentation, compliance and customer communication.
  • Identify claims leakage: overpayments, incorrect deductible, missed subrogation, unnecessary rental, repair cost inflation and authority limit breaches.
  • Check fleet-specific handling: client contract terms, multi-vehicle and driver details, cost-center allocation, reporting accuracy and special handling instructions.
  • Flag fraud indicators, complaints, bad faith exposure and unfair claims practice risks, and escalate them through the right channel.
  • Give clear, constructive feedback to adjusters and team leaders, and support coaching sessions.
  • Run calibration sessions so scoring is consistent across auditors and teams.
  • Produce monthly QA reports and dashboards covering scores, error trends, root causes and recommended actions.
  • Track corrective actions to closure and support internal, client, insurer and regulator audits.
  • Maintain QA scorecards, checklists and guidelines as products, policies and regulations change.
  • Handle claims data only in approved systems, access the minimum needed, and never copy it to unapproved tools.

Required Qualifications

  • 1-2 years in auto claims handling, claims quality assurance or insurance audit.
  • Strong knowledge of the auto claims lifecycle and terms such as indemnity, deductible, subrogation, total loss and third-party liability.
  • Experience assessing files against defined criteria, with fair and consistent judgment.
  • Working understanding of state unfair claims settlement practices acts, NAIC model regulations and bad faith standards for the states you audit.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the confidence to deliver feedback to experienced handlers.
  • Proficiency in Excel or a BI tool for scoring, sampling and trend reporting.
  • High attention to detail and the discipline to document findings so they stand up to challenge.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Fleet claims experience, including client SLAs and fleet reporting.

Values

  • We hire for drive and for fit with how we work.
  • Built around people. You make the platform easier for clients and our operations team to use. You explain what you configured in plain terms.
  • Progress through partnership. You work side by side with the product manager, engineering, and operations. You ask instead of assuming. You welcome review of your work and review others' work in return.
  • Innovation that drives real results. You look for ways to make setup faster and support tickets fewer. You do not settle for a workaround that will break next month.
  • Own the outcome. You stay with an issue until it is closed.

What we offer

  • Comprehensive benefits, including health, dental, vision insurance, and more.
    401(k) plan options
  • Paid time off, sick time, and paid holidays.
  • The opportunity to grow with a dynamic, innovative team in a startup-like culture.
Salary: $21.00 - 25.00
