jobs.excerpt: About Us: The United States has the poorest maternal and birth outcomes of all developed countries with the underserved, Black, Brown, Indigenous communities disproportionately affected.
jobs.description:
About Us:

The United States has the poorest maternal and birth outcomes of all developed countries with the underserved, Black, Brown, Indigenous communities disproportionately affected. Nadia Care is working to drastically change the experience of affected communities by reimagining how we deliver meaningful and compassionate care to expectant moms.

Nadia Care’s mission is to improve pregnancy, birth and the postpartum journey for women and their families by reimagining how maternity care is delivered. Our team is focused on building trust-based engagement and wrap-around support for expectant moms at home, in person and virtually to ensure they have all the social support they need for a successful and joyful pregnancy journey. We help our members with care navigation, doula support, assistance with lactation, nutrition, housing, transportation and a wide range of other needs. We leverage technology to support our virtual engagement that allows us to meet all our moms where they are.

We ensure that our members have trusted sources for support, resources, and information throughout their pregnancy, delivery and well into postpartum. Nadia Care does not replace the primary obstetrician or doctor’s relationships. Instead, we support expectant mothers with all other health-related social needs not typically available through their doctors’ offices.

Our Values:

  • Empathy is at the heart of everything we do. We must always center the experiences of the mothers and families we serve, as well as support and uplift one another.
  • Collaboration is what makes us stronger. We achieve the greatest impact when we work together, share knowledge, and elevate each other’s strengths.
  • Resilience reflects our ability to push through challenges, adapt in a fast-changing environment, and remain committed to our mission no matter the obstacles.

The Role:

Nadia Care is looking for a hands-on security and compliance leader to own our GovRAMP Moderate effort from start to finish. You will be our internal expert on GovRAMP, leading the security, compliance, and engineering-guidance work needed to get authorized and to stay compliant over time. Our engineering team is strong and will build everything needed, but does not have GovRAMP experience. You will close that gap by telling them what needs to be built and how to build it securely. This is an advisory role toward engineering: you will not write application code or build infrastructure yourself. You will, however, be hands-on with security work such as controls, configurations, tooling, and evidence.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead GovRAMP Moderate readiness

    • Own the GovRAMP Moderate program end to end, across security, compliance, and engineering guidance.
    • Run an internal gap assessment against GovRAMP Moderate and NIST SP 800-53 requirements.
    • Identify missing technical and administrative security controls.
    • Build and drive a prioritized remediation roadmap.
    • Define the authorization boundary and lead development of the System Security Plan (SSP) and supporting documentation.
    • Prepare the company for independent assessment and coordinate with the 3PAO.
    • Set up continuous monitoring and ongoing compliance after authorization.

    Guide engineering

    • Advise engineering on secure AWS architecture, including AWS GovCloud where needed.
    • Translate GovRAMP requirements into clear, practical technical direction.
    • Review engineering designs and proposals for security and compliance.
    • Validate that security controls are implemented correctly.

    Evaluate vendors

    • Assess current vendors and SaaS platforms for GovRAMP fit and compliance evidence.
    • Recommend which vendors can stay, which need additional controls, and which should be replaced.
    • Evaluate prospective vendors before they enter our environment.

    Own security

    • Own day-to-day security across the company: controls, monitoring, risk management, and security improvements.
    • Work with external advisors on targeted, specialized topics when needed.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in security architecture, cloud security, or security compliance.
  • Experience working at a healthcare company.
  • Proven, hands-on experience with FedRAMP Moderate or GovRAMP Moderate readiness and authorization.
  • Hands-on security experience: implementing and validating security controls, configurations, and tooling.
  • An engineering or IT infrastructure background strong enough to guide engineers on secure application and infrastructure design.
  • Strong knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 security controls.
  • Strong knowledge of AWS security architecture, including AWS GovCloud.
  • Experience running gap assessments and building remediation roadmaps.
  • Experience with SSPs, authorization boundaries, control assessments, and 3PAO coordination.
  • Experience evaluating third-party vendors and cloud service providers for compliance.
  • Understanding of continuous monitoring requirements.
  • Clear communication and the ability to work across engineering, leadership, and auditors.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Has successfully guided at least one organization through FedRAMP Moderate or GovRAMP Moderate authorization.
  • Experience with HIPAA in addition to SOC 2 and FedRAMP/GovRAMP.
  • Experience at a small or mid-sized company where you were the primary compliance owner.

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a hands-on engineering role: our engineering team owns implementation, infrastructure, and code.
  • Not a policy-only GRC role: you need real technical and hands-on security depth.

Why join us:

Working with us is a chance to build something from the ground up, shape the future of maternal health, and grow with a team that values impact, ownership, and care. As an early team member, you’ll help define how we deliver care and support at scale.

At Nadia Care, we recognize that great talent deserves great rewards. The expected base salary for this position is between $150K - $160K annually, based on relevant and direct experience.

Our Interview Process

At Nadia Care, we value transparency and want you to feel prepared at every stage of your candidate journey. Below is our standard interview process for this role:

  1. Recruiter Interview | 30 minutes
  2. Hiring Manager Interview | 1 hour
  3. Collaborator Interviews
    1. Engineering Team | 1 hour
    2. Operations | 30 minutes
  4. Executive Leadership Interview | 45 minutes

Please note that this process is subject to change, but we will always keep you informed along the way.

For full-time employees, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you both professionally and personally:

Time Off That Works for You

  • Recharge with annual paid holidays off.
  • Full-Time Salaried Employees (Exempt): Enjoy unlimited time off after the 90-day introductory period.
  • Full-Time Hourly Employees (Non-Exempt): Receive three weeks of paid time off after the 90-day introductory period.

Comprehensive Health & Wellness Coverage

  • Medical Insurance: Access top-tier healthcare, covering hospital, surgical, and prescription drug benefits. Coverage begins the first of the following month.
  • Dental Insurance: Coverage for preventive care, as well as basic and major procedures.
  • Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine eye exams and eyeglasses.

Security & Future Planning Options

  • Stock Option Grant: We believe in shared success.
  • Life Insurance: Financial protection for your beneficiaries.
  • Disability Insurance: Short-term and long-term coverage in case of illness or injury.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Opportunity to save for the future.

We’re building something great and want you to be part of it. If you're looking for a fast-paced, dynamic environment where your contributions make an impact, apply today!

Remote positions are open to candidates in the contiguous US only. Due to operational and compliance requirements, we are unable to hire candidates residing in ND, AL, HI, PR or outside the contiguous US.

Please note that our recruitment team will only contact candidates via an official company email address ending in @nadiacare.com. Be cautious of scams; Nadia Care will never ask for financial information or payments at any stage of the hiring process.

Job Description

This novel product has the potential to redefine personalized cancer treatment and requires a highly coordinated operating model to support seamless therapy delivery across a complex treatment ecosystem.

Reporting to the Director, Director, Individualized Therapy Operations, this individual serves as the commercial lead for operational demand planning, capacity planning, scenario modeling, performance management, and analytics across the Intismeran treatment ecosystem.

This leader will establish and oversee the capabilities, processes, and governance required to support operational planning, performance management, and data-driven decision making across the treatment journey. Working across Commercial, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Precision Medicine, Patient Support Programs, alliance stakeholders, and external partners, the role will translate complex operational, manufacturing, customer, and market data into actionable insights that improve operational performance, optimize resource allocation, and support strategic business decisions.

Through operational demand planning, scenario modeling, capacity management, and performance analytics, this individual will proactively identify risks and constraints, evaluate operational tradeoffs, inform alliance and business planning, and help ensure the treatment ecosystem can scale to support future growth and patient demand.

Key Responsibilities 

  • Lead the operational demand planning and capacity planning for Intismeran, developing patient volume projections, manufacturing demand assumptions, network capacity plans, and business scenarios required to support launch readiness, commercialization, and future growth.

  • Partner with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Precision Medicine, alliance stakeholders, and external partners to align projected demand with manufacturing availability, and operational readiness, proactively identifying risks and recommending mitigation strategies.

  • Develop and maintain capacity planning and scenario modeling capabilities, assessing the impact of changing demand, treatment site expansion, manufacturing constraints, and operational capacity on treatment completion and business performance.

  • Establish and oversee the operational intelligence framework for the Intismeran treatment journey, including performance dashboards, operational KPIs, demand and capacity models executive reporting, and control tower analytics that provide real-time visibility across the ecosystem.

  • Translate complex operational, logistics, manufacturing, customer, and market data into actionable business insights and strategic recommendations, enabling data-driven decision making across leadership teams and governance forums.

  • Lead operational performance management and business review processes, evaluating demand-plan assumptions, capacity utilization, treatment completion performance, operational cycle times, partner effectiveness, and overall ecosystem performance to identify improvement opportunities.

  • Drive operational excellence and continuous improvement initiatives across the treatment ecosystem, leveraging analytics and predictive insights to strengthen demand and capacity planning, optimize capacity, enhance operational efficiency, mitigate risk, and support long-term scalability.

Education:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent (BA/BS)

MBA or equivalent preferred

Required Experience and Skills:

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology industries, including experience supporting commercial organizations in operational planning, capacity planning, analytics, or treatment operations.

  • Demonstrated experience leading operational planning, capacity planning, demand planning, business analytics, or operational excellence initiatives that require coordination across multiple internal functions and external partners.

  • Experience developing and managing operational performance frameworks, including KPIs, dashboards, scorecards, business reviews, performance metrics, and executive reporting.

  • Proven ability to translate complex operational, manufacturing, customer, and market data into actionable business insights and strategic recommendations.

  • Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, with demonstrated success identifying operational risks, evaluating tradeoffs, and developing data-driven recommendations in complex environments.

  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority and effectively communicate insights and recommendations to leadership.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, balance competing priorities, and drive execution in dynamic launch, growth, or transformation environments.

About Centific

Centific is a frontier AI data foundry that curates diverse, high-quality data, using our purpose-built technology platforms to empower the Magnificent Seven and our enterprise clients with safe, scalable AI deployment. Our zero-distance innovation™ solutions for GenAI can reduce GenAI costs by up to 80% and bring solutions to market 50% faster.

Our mission is to bridge the gap between AI creators and industry leaders by bringing best practices in GenAI to unicorn innovators and enterprise customers. We aim to help these organizations unlock significant business value by deploying GenAI at scale, helping to ensure they stay at the forefront of technological advancement and maintain a competitive edge in their respective markets.

About Job

AI Research Engineer: Vision AI / VLM / Physical AI

Company: Centific

Location: Seattle, WA (or Remote)

Type: Full‑time

Build the Future of Perception & Embodied Intelligence

Are you pushing the frontier of computer vision, multimodal large models, and embodied/physical AI—and have the publications to show it? Join us to translate cutting-edge‑ research into production systems that perceive, reason, and act in the real world.

The Mission

We are building state of‑ t‑heart Vision AI across 2D/3D perception, egocentric/360° understanding, and multimodal reasoning. As an AI Research Engineer, you will own high‑ ‑leverage experiments from paper → prototype → deployable module in our platform.

We are seeking passionate Engineersto join our cutting-edge labs, you could be part of :

Computer Vision team as a Research Engineer and dive into the world of 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and visual AI. You’ll explore innovative techniques like those used to transform real-world spaces into immersive 3D models—such as the 3D Reconstruction projects —and work with cutting-edge architectures like VGG-T (Visual Geometry Grounded Transformers), known for advancing deep learning in vision tasks. This role is perfect for those excited to develop AI systems that interpret, reconstruct, and interact with the visual world, using state-of-the-art tools and methodologies. Physical AI Robotics team, where you’ll work at the intersection of simulation, robotics, and AI. You’ll leverage NVIDIA’s Omniverse for advanced 3D simulation and collaboration, Isaac Sim for robotics training and testing, and GR00T for foundation models in robotics. Experience with Holoscan SDK for real-time medical and industrial robotics pipelines, Newton Physics for dynamic simulation, and NVIDIA’s NERD for neural robot dynamics will be a plus. This role is ideal for those eager to push the boundaries of AI-driven robotics using state-of-the-art tools and frameworks.

What You’ll Do

  • Advance Visual Perception: Build and fine‑tune models for detection, tracking, segmentation (2D/3D), pose & activity recognition, and scene understanding (incl. 360° and multi‑view).
  • Multimodal Reasoning with VLMs: Train/evaluate vision–language models (VLMs) for grounding, dense captioning, temporal QA, and tooluse; design retrieval‑ augmented and agentic loops for perception‑ action‑ tasks.
  • Physical AI & Embodiment: Prototype perception‑in‑the‑loop policies that close the gap from pixels to actions (simulation + real data). Integrate with planners and task graphs for manipulation, navigation, or safety workflows.
  • Data & Evaluation at Scale: Curate datasets, author high‑signal evaluation protocols/KPIs, and run ablations that make results irreproducible impossible.
  • Systems & Deployment: Package research into reliable services on a modern stack (Kubernetes, Docker, Ray, FastAPI), with profiling, telemetry, and CI for reproducible science.
  • Agentic Workflows: Orchestrate multi-agent pipelines (e.g., ‑LangGraphstyle graphs) that combine perception, reasoning, simulation, and ‑codeg eneration to ‑selfc heck and ‑selfcorrect‑.

Example Problems You Might Tackle

  • Long horizon‑ video understanding (events, activities, causality) from egocentric or 360° video.
  • 3D scene grounding: linking language queries to objects, affordances, and trajectories.
  • Fast, privacy preserving perception for ‑ondevice‑ or edge inference.
  • Robust multi‑modal evaluation: temporal consistency, open‑set detection, uncertainty.
  • Vision conditioned‑ policy evaluation in sim (Isaac/MuJoCo) with sim2real stress tests.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Masters/Ph.D in CS/EE/Robotics (or related), actively publishing in CV/ML/Robotics (e.g., CVPR/ICCV/ECCV, NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR, CoRL/RSS).
  • Strong PyTorch (or JAX) and Python; comfort with CUDA profiling and mixed precision‑ training.
  • Demonstrated research in computer vision and at least one of: VLMs (e.g., LLaVA style, video‑ language‑ models), embodied/physical AI, 3D perception.
  • Proven ability to move from paper → code → ablation → result with rigorous experiment tracking.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with video models (e.g., TimeSFormer/MViT/VideoMAE), diffusion or 3D GS/NeRF pipelines, or SLAM/scene reconstruction.
  • Prior work on multimodal grounding (referring expressions, spatial language, affordances) or temporal reasoning.
  • Familiarity with ROS2, DeepStream/TAO, or edge inference optimizations (TensorRT, ONNX).
  • Scalable training: Ray, distributed data loaders, sharded checkpoints.
  • Strong software craft: testing, linting, profiling, containers, and reproducibility.
  • Public code artifacts (GitHub) and first‑author publications or strong open source‑ impact.

Our Stack (you’ll touch a subset)

  • Modeling: PyTorch, torchvision/lightning, Hugging Face, OpenMMLab, xFormers
  • Perception: YOLO/Detectron/MMDet, SAM/Mask2Former, CLIP‑style backbones, optical flow
  • VLM / LLM: Vision encoders + LLMs, RAG for video, toolformer‑/agent loops
  • 3D / Sim: Open3D, PyTorch3D, Isaac/MuJoCo, COLMAP/SLAM, NeRF/3DGS
  • Systems: Python, FastAPI, Ray, Kubernetes, Docker, Triton/TensorRT, Weights & Biases
  • Pipelines: LangGraph‑like orchestration, data versioning, artifact stores

What Success Looks Like

  • A publishable or open‑sourced outcome (with company approval) or a production‑ready module that measurably moves a product KPI (latency, accuracy, robustness).
  • Clean, reproducible code with documented ablations and an evaluation report that a teammate can rerun end‑to‑end.
  • A demo that clearly communicates capabilities, limits, and next steps.

Why Centific

  • Real impact: Your research ships—powering core features in our MVPs and products.
  • Mentorship: Work closely with our Principal Architect and senior engineers/researchers.
  • Velocity + Rigor: We balance top‑tier research practices with pragmatic product focus.

Salary: $90K Annually

Change Management Director – Insurance & Investments

Employment Type: Full-Time

1. Role Summary

The Change Management Director is responsible for developing and leading the organization's change management strategy to ensure successful adoption of business transformation, organizational restructuring, digital initiatives, process improvements, and strategic transformation programmes.

Within the Insurance & Investments sector, the role oversees enterprise-wide change initiatives involving operating model redesign, technology implementation, regulatory changes, organizational culture, workforce transformation, and business process modernization.

The incumbent works closely with executive leadership, HR, IT, business unit heads, and programme management teams to minimize resistance to change, strengthen organizational readiness, engage stakeholders, and ensure transformation initiatives deliver sustainable business outcomes.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Change Management Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement enterprise-wide change management strategies, frameworks, and methodologies.
  • Translate organizational transformation objectives into structured change management plans.
  • Lead change management activities across strategic programmes, projects, and business units.
  • Establish change governance structures, standards, and performance monitoring mechanisms.
  • Advise executive leadership on organizational readiness, change impacts, and adoption strategies.

B. Organizational Transformation & Change Implementation

  • Lead organizational change initiatives involving restructuring, operating model redesign, and business transformation.
  • Assess the impact of strategic changes on employees, processes, systems, and organizational structures.
  • Develop change implementation roadmaps, communication plans, and stakeholder engagement strategies.
  • Coordinate change activities across business functions to ensure consistent implementation.
  • Ensure new processes, systems, and organizational structures are effectively embedded into daily operations.

C. Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

  • Identify key stakeholders and develop targeted engagement strategies.
  • Work closely with senior management, department heads, employees, and external partners to build commitment to change.
  • Lead executive communication, employee engagement, and organizational awareness initiatives.
  • Address stakeholder concerns and manage resistance to organizational changes.
  • Establish feedback mechanisms to monitor employee sentiment and change readiness.

D. Digital & Technology Change Management

  • Lead change management activities associated with digital transformation and technology implementation.
  • Support adoption of enterprise systems, automation platforms, digital tools, and new business applications.
  • Coordinate with IT and technology teams to assess the organizational impact of system implementations.
  • Develop training programmes, user adoption strategies, and technology transition plans.
  • Monitor technology adoption and ensure employees effectively transition to new digital working practices.

E. Culture, People & Workforce Transformation

  • Partner with HR leadership to align change initiatives with workforce planning and organizational development.
  • Lead initiatives to promote cultural transformation, leadership alignment, and employee engagement.
  • Identify capability gaps and develop workforce training and development strategies.
  • Support leadership teams in managing organizational transitions and behavioral changes.
  • Promote a culture of adaptability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

F. Change Impact, Risk & Readiness Management

  • Conduct organizational change impact assessments and readiness evaluations.
  • Identify potential risks, resistance points, and implementation challenges.
  • Develop mitigation strategies and contingency plans to minimize disruption.
  • Monitor change adoption, employee engagement, and operational readiness.
  • Ensure change initiatives align with applicable insurance, investment, financial services, and regulatory requirements.

G. Benefits Realization & Performance Monitoring

  • Define change management KPIs and adoption metrics.
  • Monitor the effectiveness of change communication, training, and implementation activities.
  • Measure employee adoption, stakeholder engagement, and organizational readiness.
  • Evaluate whether transformation initiatives achieve their intended business outcomes.
  • Prepare progress reports and recommendations for executive leadership and programme steering committees.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Organizational Psychology, Management, or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree or MBA in Business Administration, Organizational Development, or Change Management is preferred.
  • 12–15+ years of progressive experience in change management, organizational transformation, business transformation, or organizational development.
  • At least 5 years in a senior change management or transformation leadership position.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-wide change initiatives within complex organizations.
  • Experience in insurance, banking, investment management, or financial services is highly desirable.
  • Strong knowledge of organizational change management, stakeholder engagement, change impact assessment, and benefits realization.
  • Experience managing change associated with digital transformation, technology implementation, restructuring, and operating model redesign.
  • Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, and executive stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Professional certifications such as Prosci Change Management, CCMP, APMG Change Management, or equivalent are advantageous.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Successful implementation of enterprise-wide change management strategies.
  • Employee adoption and engagement rates across transformation initiatives.
  • Organizational readiness and change acceptance scores.
  • Effectiveness of change communication and stakeholder engagement.
  • Completion rates of employee training and capability development programmes.
  • Reduction in resistance-related delays and implementation risks.
  • Successful adoption of new systems, processes, and operating models.
  • Achievement of transformation objectives and expected business benefits.

Senior Director, Revenue Accounting

Bitwarden is looking for a Sr. Director of Revenue Accounting to own how we recognize, record, and report revenue across both self-service and sales-assisted channels. This leader is accountable for the full revenue cycle, from contract and invoice through cash and recognized revenue. You will own our revenue stack (Stripe, HubSpot, and Rillet) end to end and partner closely with Sales, Legal, FP&A, and Engineering.

What You'll Own:

  • Own end-to-end order to cash operations for both self-service (PLG, credit card, via Stripe) and sales-assisted (enterprise, multi-year, custom contract) revenue streams.
  • Own revenue recognition under ASC 606 for self-service and sales-assisted contracts, including performance obligations, standalone selling price, contract modifications, multi-year and ramped deals, usage-based components, and channel or reseller arrangements.
  • Own deferred revenue, revenue schedules, and the monthly revenue close in Rillet, and deliver accurate revenue results to Corporate Accounting for month-end close.
  • Design billing and revenue processes for large, complex transactions: multi-entity contracts, custom pricing, mid-term upgrades and downgrades, true-ups, and co-terming, from HubSpot deal creation through Stripe invoicing to Rillet recognition.
  • Own the data flow and reconciliation across HubSpot, Stripe, and Rillet, including the bookings to billings to revenue reconciliation, the deferred revenue rollforward, and AR subledger to general ledger tie-outs.
  • Own sales tax compliance across all channels, including nexus monitoring, tax calculation and collection in Stripe, exemption certificate management, return filing and remittance, and audit readiness, in partnership with external tax advisors.
  • Write technical accounting memos for non-standard enterprise contracts and review them with external auditors.
  • Own SOX controls for the revenue cycle and serve as the main contact for audit fieldwork on revenue.
  • Define and monitor KPIs: billing accuracy, days sales outstanding, dunning/failed payment recovery rate, invoice cycle time, and dispute rates.
  • Partner with Sales to structure non-standard enterprise deals so they translate cleanly into accurate, compliant billing in Stripe.
  • Own sales commission accounting and administration, including commission calculations and payouts, ASC 340-40 capitalization and amortization of commission costs, and accrual accuracy, and partner with Sales leadership, FP&A, and HR on commission plan design, quota and attainment rules, and the cost and controls impact of plan changes.
  • Drive Stripe configuration and automation (subscription schedules, proration rules, dunning/failed payment recovery, invoicing rules) to reduce manual touch on high-volume self-service billing.
  • Partner with SalesOps to own the HubSpot-to-Stripe-to-Rillet data pipeline — ensuring deal terms, billing events, and revenue entries stay in sync, and closing gaps with native integrations, middleware, or custom tooling as needed.
  • Collaborate with Product/Engineering on Stripe/product OTC enhancements, new pricing models, and packaging changes.
  • Lead, mentor, and scale a billing, collections and commission teams (analysts, specialists, managers) as transaction volume and deal complexity grow.

What We're Looking For:

  • 10+ years of accounting experience, including 5+ years in SaaS revenue accounting and 3+ years leading teams.
  • CPA or equivalent public accounting experience
  • Deep, hands-on ASC 606 experience for SaaS, including large and non-standard enterprise transactions: custom terms, multi-year deals, usage-based or hybrid pricing, amendments, and co-terming.
  • Experience accounting for both self-service (high-volume, automated, credit-card-based) and sales-assisted (contract-based, high-value) revenue.
  • Experience with SOX, external audit management, and building controls in a growing company.
  • Experience managing billing, collections, or order-to-cash teams, and commission
  • Track record of building scalable processes and automating manual workflows, including integrations between CRM, billing, and accounting systems.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable in ambiguity and fast-changing environments.

In the United States, the starting base compensation range for this role is $200,000 - $225,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, relevant experience, and skill set as assessed in the interview process, as well as market data by location. See our careers page for a list of benefits.

The Transformation Director is responsible for leading and driving enterprise-wide transformation initiatives to improve organizational performance, operational efficiency, business growth, customer experience, and long-term competitiveness.

Within the Insurance & Investments sector, the role oversees strategic transformation programmes involving digital innovation, business process reengineering, operating model redesign, technology modernization, organizational restructuring, regulatory compliance, and cultural change.

The incumbent works closely with executive leadership, business unit heads, technology teams, and external partners to translate corporate strategy into actionable transformation initiatives, ensuring measurable business outcomes, sustainable change adoption, and improved organizational performance.

A. Enterprise Transformation Strategy

  • Develop and execute the organization's enterprise-wide transformation strategy and roadmap.

  • Align transformation priorities with business strategy, market developments, customer expectations, and regulatory requirements.
  • Advise the CEO and executive leadership on transformation priorities, investment decisions, and strategic opportunities.

  • Lead digital transformation initiatives involving automation, cloud adoption, data analytics, artificial intelligence, and enterprise technology modernization.
  • Oversee the implementation of digital platforms, business applications, and technology-enabled operating models.

  • Promote digital innovation across insurance operations, investment management, customer services, and distribution channels.

  • Monitor programme milestones, budgets, risks, dependencies, and expected business benefits.

  • Ensure transformation initiatives are delivered within approved timelines, budgets, and quality expectations.

E. Financial Performance & Value Creation

  • Develop transformation business cases, investment proposals, and financial impact assessments.

  • Monitor transformation expenditure, financial benefits, and return on investment.
  • Establish benefits realization frameworks to measure the financial and operational impact of transformation initiatives.

  • Work with HR and business leaders to develop change communication, training, and employee engagement initiatives.
  • Build organizational readiness and address resistance to change.
  • Promote a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

This role is key to introducing Scene services to potential patient members for enrollment. The enrollment specialist must excel at connecting with the patient via phone and discovering what patients need through outbound communication. Once patient needs are identified, we rely on the Outbound Enrollment Specialist to guide and direct patients into our services ecosystem. jobs.excerpt: PSI CRO is looking for an experienced finance professional in the Clinical Research industry, who will be responsible for managing clinical project budgeting, negotiating, and analyzing budgets, as well as providing support with proposals and contract management activities within the company.
jobs.description:
PSI CRO is looking for an experienced finance professional in the Clinical Research industry, who will be responsible for managing clinical project budgeting, negotiating, and analyzing budgets, as well as providing support with proposals and contract management activities within the company.

Full-time employment based in Canada

Responsibilities:

  • Development of study budget (preparation of budgets for proposals and Change Order budgets for on-going projects)
  • Management of study budget throughout the clinical project duration (setup and maintenance of project finance information in PSI internal systems, preparation of accrual reports, request for invoices)
  • Development of Sponsor Contract (preparation of sponsor agreements and change orders, development of payment schedules)
  • Timesheet System Management (setup and maintenance of project-specific timesheets in PSI’s internal system, management of reconciliation of actual vs budget costs on a regular basis)
  • Experience in global study budgeting & contract management within a CRO/Pharma
  • Education in Finance/Economics or commensurate and relevant training
  • Experience in project budgeting, budget negotiation, budget analysis (actual vs. planned), forecasts, project scope management, mapping to different budget grids
  • Knowledge of time tracking systems and budgeting systems/tools
  • Computer literacy, professional/advanced user of MS Excel
  • Ability to produce accurate and timely information/ finance reports
  • Analytical skills
  • Communication/negotiation skills; ability to train others
  • Organizational and time management skills

Advance your career in clinical research and lead challenging full-service projects on the country/regional level while growing with a rapid company, that puts its people first! You will get hands-on involvement in every aspect of the study.

PSI is a leading Contract Research Organization (CRO) with 30 years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry. Originated in Switzerland, PSI is a privately owned, full-service CRO with a global reach, supporting clinical trials across multiple countries and continents. Our reputation for being highly selective about the projects we undertake highlights our commitment to delivering high-quality, timely services across a broad spectrum of therapeutic indications.

At PSI, we foster an environment where a diverse range of colleagues feel welcomed and valued. Our inclusive culture is a cornerstone of our success, enabling us to attract and retain top talent globally.

We are not just about conducting clinical trials; we are about building a community where every team member has the opportunity to thrive and contribute to groundbreaking advancements in the pharmaceutical industry.

jobs.title: Director of Powerbuilding
jobs.excerpt: Who Are We Kairos is working for liberation at the intersection of technology, racial justice, and democracy by building a world where tech works for all.
jobs.description:
Who Are We

Kairos is working for liberation at the intersection of technology, racial justice, and democracy by building a world where tech works for all. Technology can–and should–be used to improve the quality of life for all people without being at the expense of others and the environment. We believe that people have the authority and agency to determine how technology intersects with their everyday lives.

We organize, train, educate, convene and support everyday people as they develop capacity and skills to combat authoritarian technology at local and state levels. We also create pathways for people to share skills and learnings from their local contexts.

Our organizational values are: Interdependent Leadership, No Lone Wolves, Principled Struggle, Durability, Curiosity and Care, Fighting for Black and Trans Liberation, Resiliency, Growth Oriented, Rigor and Discipline, and Technology Is Not Neutral. To be successful, we challenge ourselves to live our values and vision as we build the world we want. Joy, laughter, fun, and rigor are the ingredients we include as we work toward our vision together.

Kairos is a remote, nimble, and growing team. Our team consists of ten full-time staff persons and a few contractors, with collaborative input and clear decision-makers. We are still growing and learning and are looking for someone who will dive in and help shape our work for years to come.

Overview of the Role

The Director of PowerBuilding is responsible to lead the Power Building team & execute the overall Power Building strategy and campaign planning with deep orientation toward base-building. They will provide key thought partnership to the Executive and Leads team and will be instrumental in cultivating external partnerships.

The Director of PowerBuilding will report directly to the Executive Director and will work collaboratively with everyone on the team. We are aiming for this position to begin in February 2027.

A strong candidate for this position is an expert strategist, a relationship builder, and is deeply experienced in base-building.

Salary & Benefits:

This is a full-time, exempt position. Kairos staff work roughly 40 hours a week, understanding that the schedule must flex to accommodate the necessary ebbs and flows of the work along with everyday life, such as multi-day trainings, breaking news moments that are crucial for our communities, and personal matters that may require a shift in regular working hours.

The salary for this position starts at $113,000 and increases from there based on years of prior experience. Basing compensation on someone’s willingness and ability to negotiate or on their prior pay rates leads to vast inequities and bias in how people are paid, particularly for groups experiencing historical oppression. Therefore, we do not ask for prior pay history from our candidates, and our offer-making process is negotiation-free. We also have a progressive compensation philosophy that guides salary increases and role promotions for our staff.

Our salary and benefits are an extension of our organizational values, and we endeavor to remain competitive while centering the humanity and needs of our people. To that end, our benefits package includes generous vacation (including three weeks of office closures each year); full health, dental, vision and flex benefits; 403b retirement match plan; ongoing training opportunities; funds for home office set-up and professional development.

Schedule:

The role is a full time, 40 hours per week position. Occasional evenings and weekend work hours may be needed.

Location:

As we are a distributed team, your primary residence may be located anywhere in the United States. This role may require moderate levels of travel to connect with partners and internal stakeholders. Organization-sponsored travel for conferences, Kairos’ trainings, partner meetings, and face-to-face staff gatherings is required.

Responsibilities

Lead & Execute Strategy and Campaigning(40%)

  • Develop, regularly evaluate, and track the PowerBuilding team’s strategy in alignment with organizational strategy, and in collaboration with key internal stakeholders. This will include:

    • Deepen the team strategy to build a base around campaigns that connect resisting Big Tech influence to building alternatives, with a clear vision for everyday people’s agency and self-determination around technology.

    • Popular political education and capacity building for grassroots partners to build space for advocacy around Big Tech at the local, state, and national level.

  • Build long-term relationships with local partners and national cross-movement organizations to deepen the analysis of Kairos’ work, and ensure that Kairos’ base building and organizing continues to orient towards impact.

  • Identify & lead rapid response efforts in coordination with Director of Communications & Director of Digital Projects.

Team Management (40%)

  • Supervise and support our three-member organizing team (and others as the team grows).

  • Oversee the progress of the team work plan, budget, campaign plans, and individual staff plans.

  • Establish standardized mechanisms for management, tracking, and assessment of campaigns for the full team.

  • Lead by example in building the Kairos culture, team spirit, ethos, and organizational strategy, including quarterly and yearly planning.

  • Draft partner agreements and MOUs for executive approval.

  • Maintain separation of 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) activity, in collaboration with Chief of Staff and Director of Operations.

    Thought Leadership & External Positioning (20%)

  • Engage in public speaking, writing, and media, lifting up the work of Kairos.

  • Provide strategic thought partnership and collaborative visioning as a member of the Kairos leads team.

  • Partner with Executive Director and Director of Development with identifying and cultivating potential key funder opportunities & relationships; champion Kairos’ work in ways that invite new funding sources.

Requirements

Role Specific Required Skills, Abilities, Training and Experience:

  • A movement builder with 5-7 years of union and/or community experience, holding deep ties to communities of color. Strong preference for community or union organizing over electoral campaign organizing.

  • Robust (4+ years) campaign leadership experience (has run campaigns toward impact & depth) + managed others in planning and running campaigns toward the same.

  • Oriented toward developing organizers (not just day-to-day management; hold deep clarity about growth edges & developing leaders).

  • Able to develop, lead, and adjust strategy in real time.

Generally required skills for all Directors

  • Can translate field observations into actionable programs and work plans.

  • An exceptional listener; a strategic, collaborative, and imaginative problem-solver.

  • Demonstrated high-level project management skills; skilled at managing multiple projects simultaneously.

  • Able to remain poised and effective while juggling competing priorities under pressure.

  • Direct and collaboration-oriented communicator, able to manage group dynamics to move discussions toward decisions and action.

  • Self-reflective, able to receive and implement feedback, self-motivated, disciplined, and rigorous.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Can think through & lead change management.

  • Fluency in digital organizing and integrated strategy.

  • Builds and holds key relationships within the field; networks & power-maps.

  • Can identify key partnerships & spaces where they think Kairos should be.

Competencies Expected:

Job duties describe what each role must do. Competencies are the knowledge, skills, and abilities needed to be successful in doing those duties. Of the following competencies, everyone, regardless of position, will have different strengths and growth edges. All staff are expected to strive to be competent in all of these dimensions, but expectations increase as seniority, responsibilities, and management responsibilities increase.

Understand the overall organizational vision, values, and culture; team’s area of work; and the field of play.

  • Every staff person needs to understand the following aspects of our work:

    • Overall organizational vision, values, and culture (including Kairos theory of change, strategy, goals, and how they add up to long term vision as well as practices that ensure values and culture are )

    • Principles that animate their team’s work (e.g., everyone on the organizing team needs to understand organizing principles and organizing online; everyone on campaigns needs to understand campaigning principles and online campaigning; everyone on operations needs to understand operations functions, etc.)

    • What is happening the field relevant to our work and the kind of intervention Kairos makes or should make to add value to the field

  • The level of understanding necessary to perform the role changes with seniority and responsibility,

    • Entry level positions require a basic understanding

    • Early level career positions require a working and applicable understanding

    • Mid level career positions require a thorough, applicable, and adaptable understanding

    • Senior level career positions require a comprehensive understanding, evolving and sharpening the organization’s understanding, and the ability to teach and coach others as they grow in their understanding

Able to manage projects effectively

  • Every staff member is expected to manage projects for which they are responsible. This includes:

    • Hitting milestones and final deliverables on time, with attention to detail and meeting strategic purposes of the project.

    • Communicating effectively about status to relevant colleagues and stakeholders.

    • Using judgment to prioritize and work effectively and strategically to reach goals, spotting obstacles in advance, and recommending solutions as needed.

    • Exercising resiliency when problems come up and using judgment about when to ask for help

  • The scope of the projects staff are expected to take changes with seniority and responsibility.

    • Entry and early career level staff are expected to manage discrete projects, with support initially, but moving towards independence as they become familiar with their role

    • Mid level career staff are expected to manage large projects with complexity and many moving parts (people, orgs, events), with support initially, but moving towards independence; they may also simultaneously be managing other staff who are managing discrete projects.

    • Senior level staff are expected to manage multiple projects at time, and support other managing projects of their own, as they consider the whole of the organization.

Give and receive feedback

  • Every staff person is expected to give feedback respectfully and strategically, receive feedback gracefully, adapt based on feedback.

  • The skill with which one gives and receives feedback is expected to change with seniority and responsibility

    • Entry, early, and mid level staff are expected to invite feedback, respond to it, and provide it to colleagues constructively, to help everyone grow in their work and the organization evolve.

    • Senior level staff are expected to model feedback exchanges, coach others in how to give and receive feedback, and collaboratively develop practices that set organizational conditions for a feedback rich environment.

Exercise Anticipatory Thinking and Visioning (Strategic Thinking)

Every staff person is expected to understand the following aspects of our work

  • Entry and early career staff are expected to reflect on past work, eco-system developments, and bring learnings from the work to future projects and tasks.

  • Mid level career staff are expected to consistently and independently evaluate and understand the impact of a project or task as it relates to team and organizational goals and TOC, envision how the impact would change based on adjustments to future projects or tasks, and take learnings from work in real time and make iterations in the moment.

  • Senior level staff are expected to collaborate across teams and build out strong and clear strategies for big bodies of work (e.g., a team’s work, a major long-term project) that align with overall organizational goals and TOC, and incorporate an external analysis of the movement and moment into their vision, and provide strong insight and develop proposals on how that should impact our work going forward.

Physical Requirements:

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with different abilities to perform the essential functions.

  • This position requires prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

  • This position requires being able to read a computer screen & ability to utilize a phone for communication.

Wellness Policy

Kairos is committed to cultivating situations where people feel safe, respected, and well - physically, emotionally, and relationally - when we gather in person. We recognize that gathering matters. It strengthens our relationships, deepens our collaboration, and supports the kind of connection that sustains our work.

At the same time, we acknowledge that we are navigating an ongoing reality of COVID-19 and other illnesses. Our approach is grounded in shared responsibility, informed choice, and community care. This means we ask more of one another as we practice awareness, communication, and care in community. As a community, we commit to:

  • Showing care for ourselves and one another

  • Staying attuned to our bodies and any symptoms of illness

  • Communicating openly and honestly when we are not feeling well

  • Respecting different comfort levels, access needs, and personal boundaries

  • Making thoughtful choices that support both individual and collective well-being

EEOC Statement

Kairos Fellowship is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, creed, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, ethnicity, national origin, immigration status, sexual orientation, religion, HIV serostatus, disability, height, weight, veteran status or marital status.

We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign-born residents, people of all ages, and veterans to apply, even if they don’t see themselves in every requirement or competency. We are committed to building a team that is inclusive of a variety of backgrounds and perspectives.

Application Process:

  • Kairos receives an extraordinary amount of applications, therefore we commit to personally reviewing the first 150 applications.

  • Application Deadline: December 18 (unless we receive 150 applications prior to this date).

  • We review resumes and applications to learn what we need to know about applicants; a cover letter is not necessary.

Highlights

Expert strategist, a relationship builder, and is deeply experienced in base-building.

We are seeking an experienced Infrastructure Platform Technical Lead to lead the design, delivery and support of enterprise infrastructure and platform services, with a strong focus on VMware and Red Hat OpenShift.

The organisation's technology estate is primarily on-premises, therefore strong enterprise infrastructure experience is essential. You will provide technical leadership across infrastructure, virtualisation, platform engineering and automation initiatives, ensuring solutions are secure, resilient, scalable and operationally supportable.

Working closely with architects, engineers, application teams, security teams and suppliers, you will drive technical governance, solution design, operational excellence and modernisation across the infrastructure estate. Whilst the role is infrastructure-focused, experience designing and supporting cloud-native architectures and containerised platforms is required to support ongoing transformation initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, delivery and support of enterprise infrastructure and platform solutions.
  • Provide technical leadership across VMware, OpenShift and core infrastructure technologies.
  • Drive technical governance, design assurance and engineering best practices.
  • Ensure solutions are secure, resilient, highly available and operationally supportable.
  • Champion automation, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and continuous improvement.
  • Manage technical risks, dependencies and stakeholder engagement.
  • Mentor engineering teams and coordinate specialist technical resources.

Essential

  • Proven experience in an Infrastructure Platform Technical Lead, Infrastructure Technical Lead or similar senior technical role.
  • Strong expertise in VMware enterprise virtualisation platforms.
  • Hands-on experience with Red Hat OpenShift and Kubernetes platform administration.
  • Strong background supporting large-scale on-premises enterprise infrastructure environments.
  • Experience with RHEL, enterprise storage, backup and disaster recovery solutions.
  • Experience delivering highly available, resilient and secure production platforms.
  • Knowledge of automation technologies including Ansible, Terraform and Infrastructure as Code.
  • Experience designing and supporting cloud-native architectures, container platforms and modern application hosting models.
  • Strong understanding of operational readiness, platform support and service reliability.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.

Desirable

  • Azure and/or AWS hybrid cloud environments
  • Ansible Automation Platform
  • ArgoCD and GitOps practices
  • Prometheus, Grafana and enterprise observability platforms
  • Platform Engineering and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices

Ideal Candidate A hands-on technical leader with deep VMware and OpenShift expertise, capable of leading the evolution of a predominantly on-premises infrastructure estate while leveraging cloud-native architecture principles, automation and modern platform engineering practices.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer – AI Platform Architecture
jobs.excerpt: Enquadramento da Função Procuramos um Principal Engineer – AI Platform Architecture para assumir responsabilidades na definição, evolução e governação da arquitetura técnica de uma plataforma de procurement baseada em Inteligência Artificial, assegurando a escalabilidade, fiabilidade e consistência das soluções tecnológicas.
jobs.description:
Enquadramento da Função

Procuramos um Principal Engineer – AI Platform Architecture para assumir responsabilidades na definição, evolução e governação da arquitetura técnica de uma plataforma de procurement baseada em Inteligência Artificial, assegurando a escalabilidade, fiabilidade e consistência das soluções tecnológicas.

A função combina conhecimentos avançados de Software Architecture, Distributed Systems e Cloud-Native Engineering com competências de definição de padrões arquiteturais, integração de agentes de Inteligência Artificial e desenvolvimento de capacidades tecnológicas reutilizáveis.

O profissional terá um papel central na definição da direção arquitetural da plataforma, estabelecendo a forma como agentes autónomos, serviços de orquestração, APIs, sistemas distribuídos, ferramentas de desenvolvimento e mecanismos de observabilidade se integram numa arquitetura coerente e sustentável.

Trata-se de uma função de liderança técnica com forte componente prática, orientada para a definição de arquiteturas, padrões de engenharia e evolução tecnológica da plataforma, sem responsabilidades diretas de gestão hierárquica de equipas.

Principais Responsabilidades

  • Definir, desenvolver e evoluir a arquitetura técnica de uma plataforma de Inteligência Artificial, assegurando o suporte a aplicações inteligentes e soluções de procurement;
  • Estabelecer padrões arquiteturais reutilizáveis para orquestração de agentes de IA, execução de workflows, integração de ferramentas, gestão de memória e contexto e serviços de plataforma;
  • Definir standards de engenharia para APIs, sistemas distribuídos, observabilidade, testes, deployment, documentação e excelência operacional;
  • Orientar decisões arquiteturais em colaboração com equipas de Product Engineering, Platform Engineering, Data, Security e Product Management;
  • Contribuir para a evolução do Agentic Software Development Lifecycle (ASDLC), promovendo a integração de automação e agentes autónomos nos processos de desenvolvimento de software;
  • Identificar e desenvolver capacidades tecnológicas reutilizáveis que reduzam a duplicação de soluções e acelerem a disponibilização de funcionalidades;
  • Rever desenhos técnicos e arquiteturas de soluções, fornecendo orientações técnicas para iniciativas de elevada complexidade;
  • Colaborar com equipas de engenharia na definição de soluções que conciliem a evolução tecnológica de longo prazo com as necessidades de implementação de produtos;
  • Avaliar tecnologias, frameworks e abordagens arquiteturais emergentes, identificando oportunidades de adoção com valor mensurável e evitando complexidade desnecessária;
  • Apoiar o desenvolvimento técnico de engenheiros séniores através de Design Reviews, Technical Coaching e orientação arquitetural;
  • Promover boas práticas de Engenharia de Software que melhorem a experiência dos developers, a fiabilidade, a escalabilidade e a eficiência operacional da plataforma;
  • Assegurar a consistência das decisões arquiteturais entre diferentes equipas e componentes tecnológicos;
  • Contribuir para a evolução contínua dos padrões de desenvolvimento, integração e manutenção de sistemas;
  • Promover arquiteturas seguras, observáveis e adaptáveis à evolução das tecnologias de Inteligência Artificial.

Requisitos

  • Experiência comprovada no desenho e desenvolvimento de plataformas de software de grande escala e sistemas distribuídos;
  • Conhecimentos avançados de arquiteturas de aplicações Cloud-Native e práticas modernas de Engenharia de Software;
  • Experiência na definição e implementação de standards técnicos e arquiteturais transversais a diferentes equipas de engenharia;
  • Experiência sólida em Software Engineering, incluindo desenvolvimento de componentes e capacidades de plataforma reutilizáveis;
  • Conhecimentos práticos de Microservices, APIs, sistemas assíncronos e arquiteturas Event-Driven;
  • Experiência na definição e orientação de decisões arquiteturais em ambientes tecnológicos complexos;
  • Experiência na orientação técnica e mentoria de engenheiros séniores, através de liderança técnica e sem dependência de responsabilidades de gestão hierárquica;
  • Capacidade de colaboração com equipas de Infrastructure, Applications, AI Systems e Product Engineering;
  • Conhecimentos de práticas de desenvolvimento que promovam escalabilidade, fiabilidade, segurança e manutenção das soluções;
  • Capacidade de analisar problemas técnicos complexos e transformá-los em padrões arquiteturais claros, consistentes e escaláveis;
  • Experiência na revisão de desenhos técnicos e definição de orientações arquiteturais;
  • Excelente capacidade de comunicação e influência técnica junto de equipas multidisciplinares;
  • Capacidade de articular decisões técnicas com necessidades de negócio e objetivos de desenvolvimento de produto;
  • Autonomia na definição de soluções e tomada de decisões arquiteturais;
  • Capacidade de análise crítica e resolução de problemas técnicos complexos;
  • Compromisso com a qualidade, consistência e evolução sustentável das soluções tecnológicas.

Valorizamos

  • Experiência em arquiteturas de plataformas que integrem agentes autónomos de Inteligência Artificial;
  • Conhecimentos de Agent Orchestration, Workflow Execution e Context Management;
  • Familiaridade com o conceito de Agentic Software Development Lifecycle (ASDLC);
  • Experiência na definição de padrões de integração e reutilização de serviços em plataformas tecnológicas;
  • Conhecimentos de práticas de automação aplicadas ao ciclo de desenvolvimento de software;
  • Experiência na avaliação e adoção de tecnologias e frameworks emergentes;
  • Experiência na melhoria da Developer Experience e na evolução de práticas de Engenharia de Software;
  • Capacidade de equilibrar decisões arquiteturais de longo prazo com necessidades imediatas de desenvolvimento e implementação.

Perfil Procurado

Procuramos um profissional com elevada maturidade técnica em Software Architecture e Engenharia de Sistemas Distribuídos, capaz de definir a direção arquitetural de plataformas tecnológicas complexas e assegurar a consistência das soluções desenvolvidas por diferentes equipas.

Deverá combinar uma visão estratégica da arquitetura tecnológica com capacidade de intervenção técnica, demonstrando autonomia na definição de padrões, avaliação de soluções e orientação de decisões arquiteturais.

A capacidade de influenciar tecnicamente equipas multidisciplinares, simplificar problemas complexos e promover a reutilização de componentes será essencial, assim como o rigor na definição de standards e a preocupação com a escalabilidade, segurança e manutenção das soluções.

Valorizamos um perfil analítico, pragmático e orientado para a excelência técnica, com capacidade de liderança através do conhecimento, mentoria e colaboração, contribuindo para a evolução sustentável de plataformas de Inteligência Artificial e para a melhoria contínua das práticas de engenharia.

jobs.title: In-House CRA II (Mexico)
jobs.excerpt: We’re expanding across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile and Peru, and we’re looking for an experienced In-house CRA II to help build the foundation of this new regional function in Mexico!
jobs.description:
We’re expanding across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile and Peru, and we’re looking for an experienced In-house CRA II to help build the foundation of this new regional function in Mexico!

The In-house CRA II provides overall support to study sites and clinical project teams engaged in clinical research studies. You will adhere to applicable protocols, standard operating procedures (SOPs) and all applicable guidelines and regulatory requirements (e.g., International Council for Harmonization (ICH), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and country/region-specific regulations). Acts as point of contact for study sites.

The In-house CRA ll is a solid team member who can execute all core responsibilities consistently across several studies using independent judgment and critical thinking. Individual works independently as study team member with minimum support in complex activities.

Essential functions of the job included but not limited to:

  • Assist with the investigator recruitment activities utilizing phone scripts, questionnaires, study site materials and other tools for use in evaluating investigative sites
  • May assist in identifying study sites by performing site feasibility and recruitment tasks, e.g., completing, disseminating, and reviewing responses to site recruitment questionnaires
  • Schedules internal and external meetings as required
  • Prepares Investigator Site Files including distribution to study sites (electronically or physically), coordination with shipping vendor, if required
  • Performs ongoing essential document collection and review, maintenance, and close-out activities, organizing and maintaining site level data in the trial master file (TMF) under general supervision ensuring that sponsor and investigator obligations are being met and are compliant with ICH/GCP guidelines and applicable local regulations
  • Assist with set ups and maintains site-related data in applicable clinical systems according to procedures and guidelines Utilizes the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) to ensure milestones and activities are accurately tracked
  • Acts as site contact/liaison for study and site management issues including addressing questions, assists with managing study supplies, and may support offsite central monitoring activities. Escalates issues and risks as needed
  • Ensures timely and complete data entry by site in EDC or any other system that requires data entry

¡Hola! Somos Cashea 👋 y nuestra misión es devolverle a los venezolanos la oportunidad de acceder al crédito a través de un modelo de negocios BNPL. Desde nuestro lanzamiento en 2022, nos hemos dedicado a promover la inclusión financiera. Hoy día tenemos más de 11 millones de usuarios activos, tanto para consumidores como para comercios, y nos hemos convertido en una marca de confianza en Venezuela, conquistando mentes y corazones

Resumen del role

Buscamos un Analista Financiero para Cashea, una fintech en crecimiento. La posición tendrá como foco principal la planificación financiera y el análisis del negocio, y apoyará las actividades de investor relations y la preparación de materiales para la gerencia, el directorio e inversionistas.

Formará parte del equipo de Finanzas Estratégicas y trabajará en modelos, proyecciones y análisis que permitan entender el desempeño de la compañía, evaluar oportunidades y apoyar decisiones de crecimiento, financiamiento y asignación de capital.Si esto resuena contigo, ¡sigue leyendo!

Responsabilidades

  • Apoyar los procesos de planificación financiera, presupuesto y actualización de proyecciones de la compañía.

  • Desarrollar y mantener modelos financieros para proyectar resultados, flujos de caja y necesidades de capital.

  • Analizar el desempeño financiero y operativo, explicar desviaciones frente al plan e identificar riesgos y oportunidades.

  • Realizar análisis de negocio y rentabilidad para apoyar la evaluación de productos, iniciativas y nuevas oportunidades de crecimiento.

  • Preparar análisis de escenarios y sensibilidad para evaluar el impacto de distintos supuestos en los resultados y la posición financiera.

  • Apoyar análisis de costo de capital, alternativas de financiamiento y asignación de recursos.

  • Preparar reportes, presentaciones y otros materiales financieros para la gerencia, el directorio e inversionistas.

  • Apoyar las actividades de investor relations, incluyendo la actualización de información financiera y la atención de requerimientos de inversionistas y potenciales proveedores de capital.

  • Colaborar con distintas áreas para consolidar información y mejorar los procesos de análisis y reporte financiero.

Requisitos

  • Título universitario en Economía, Finanzas, Contaduría, Ingeniería o carrera afín.

  • De 1 a 4 años de experiencia en planificación financiera, finanzas corporativas o consultoría financiera.

  • Conocimientos sólidos de finanzas corporativas, planificación y análisis financiero.

  • Comprensión de los estados financieros y su relación con el desempeño del negocio.

  • Excel avanzado y experiencia en modelación financiera.

  • Capacidad para trabajar con datos, identificar tendencias y convertir hallazgos en conclusiones útiles para el negocio.

  • Dominio avanzado de inglés y español, con capacidad para hablar, leer y escribir en ambos idiomas, participar en reuniones y preparar materiales financieros.

  • Habilidad para preparar presentaciones y comunicar información financiera de forma clara y estructurada.

  • Capacidad analítica, atención al detalle y organización para manejar varias prioridades.

  • Criterio para cuestionar supuestos, validar resultados y trabajar con distintas áreas de la compañía.

Por qué te encantará trabajar en Cashea

En Cashea tenemos una cultura de trabajo basada en la confianza y el propósito. Si necesitas una pista de por qué somos una buena opción, estos son nuestros valores fundamentales:

  • No trabajamos en piloto automático. Todo lo que hacemos es intencional. Nos encanta elaborar ideas plenamente conscientes del impacto que pueden tener en nuestros usuarios.

  • Tu creatividad y curiosidad son el activo más Importante.

  • Tu voz importa. Escuchamos y damos espacio a las ideas y al feedback. Todos pertenecen y lo que es importante para ti, también lo es para nosotros.

  • Valoramos la transparencia. La claridad nos mantiene conectados y con los pies en la tierra.

  • Por último, pero no menos importante, nos enfocamos en el impacto real.

Si quieres trabajar con nosotros, llena la aplicación. ¡Nos encantaría conocerte!

jobs.description:
FDNA is a pioneer in AI-powered phenotyping and precision health, dedicated to expediting the diagnosis and care management of rare genetic and developmental disorders. Used across more than 10,000 medical centers in over 130 countries, our ecosystem and products bridges the gap between concerned parents, healthcare providers, and life sciences organization.

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic, execution-driven Head of Product based in Latin America to own the end-to-end product vision, roadmap, and delivery across FDNA’s clinical, patient-facing, and interoperability product lines. Reporting directly to the executive leadership team (working closely with our Chief Product & Technology Officer, Chief Medical Officer, and AI Research leads), you will translate cutting-edge multimodal AI capabilities into intuitive, compliant, and clinically impactful products tailored primarily for the US healthcare ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy & Lifecycle Ownership: Define and execute the multi-product roadmap across Face2Gene, Family Health Checker, and FDNA’s Provider/Pharma Data Clearinghouse, balancing clinician utility, patient engagement, and B2B/life sciences monetization.
  • US Clinical Workflow & EHR Integration: Architect seamless product experiences that fit naturally into US pediatric, genetic, and primary care clinical workflows, driving HL7/FHIR-based EHR integrations, digital intake, and specialist referral pathways.
  • Regulatory & Compliance Governance: Partner with Legal, Clinical, and Security teams to ensure all product features strictly adhere to HIPAA privacy/security mandates, de-identification protocols, and FDA Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) / Clinical Decision Support (CDS) regulatory boundaries.
  • AI-to-Product Translation: Collaborate closely with AI/ML engineering and medical genetics teams to productize novel multimodal models (facial analysis, video, audio, and clinical notes) while maintaining high standards for clinical transparency, bias mitigation, and explainability.
  • Cross-Functional & Nearshore Leadership: Lead, mentor, and scale a distributed product management and UX/UI design function across time zones, fostering tight alignment between LATAM-based teams, US-based commercial/clinical stakeholders, and global R&D centers.
  • Customer & Market Discovery: Conduct continuous discovery with US health systems, pediatric specialists, genetic counselors, patient advocacy groups, and pharma/CRO partners to validate product-market fit and measure clinical and commercial outcomes.

Requirements

- Experience:6+ years of progressive product management experience, including at least 2+ years in a senior leadership role (Director or Head of Product) owning multiple interconnected software products.

- Dedicated US Healthcare Exposure (Mandatory):≥50% of your career (3+ years minimum) must be directly dedicated to building and scaling products for the US healthcare market, demonstrating hands-on mastery of:

  • HIPAA Compliance & Data Privacy: Managing PHI/PII, BAAs, SOC 2 standards, and de-identified real-world data (RWD) exchange.
  • FDA & SaMD Parameters: Navigating FDA guidance on Clinical Decision Support (CDS) software, SaMD classifications, and non-diagnostic informational labeling.
  • US EHR Integrations: Hands-on experience shipping integrations with major US EHRs (e.g., Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth) utilizing HL7, FHIR, SMART on FHIR, or clearinghouse APIs.
  • US Clinical Workflows: Deep familiarity with US provider intake, referral management, care coordination, and specialty clinical environments.

- Location & Alignment: Residing in any Latin American country with strong overlap with US Eastern/Central business hours and fluent, executive-level English communication skills.

- AI / Data-Intensive Product Track Record: Proven experience bringing data-heavy, algorithmic, or AI/ML-powered healthcare applications from concept to commercial adoption.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience with rare diseases, clinical genomics, pediatrics, digital diagnostics, or life sciences/CRO real-world data platforms.
  • Background working in high-growth healthtech startups or distributed international R&D organizations.
  • Familiarity with consumer-to-provider ("digital front door") patient acquisition and engagement funnels.

CV/Resume submissions MUST be in English.
