Director, Contract Strategy & Operations


About The Office of the Chief Procurement Officer

The Office of the Chief Procurement Officer (OCPO) provides strategic leadership and oversight for Cornell University's procurement, supplier management, payment operations, travel and expense, and related business services. OCPO is responsible for developing and implementing procurement strategies, policies, systems, and processes that support the university's academic, research, clinical, and administrative missions. Through collaboration with stakeholders across Cornell University and Weill Cornell Medicine, OCPO drives operational excellence, supplier value, compliance, risk management, and responsible stewardship of institutional resources.


The contracting function reports to the Executive Director, Category Management serves as Cornell's Center of Excellence (COE) for supplier contracting, providing governance, policy oversight, contract lifecycle management, operational support, and technology enablement across Cornell University and Weill Cornell Medicine. Through the administration of enterprise contracting processes, stakeholder engagement, and partnership with the Office of General Counsel, Risk Management, Information Security, Privacy, Compliance, and other institutional stakeholders, the team promotes efficient, transparent, and risk-informed contracting practices while continuously advancing Cornell's contract management capabilities.


The Opportunity

Transform enterprise contracting at one of the world's premier academic institutions.

Cornell University is seeking a visionary and strategic leader to serve as our Director, Contract Strategy & Operations. This is a rare opportunity to build and lead a next-generation contract management program that supports Cornell's far-reaching mission across education, groundbreaking research, healthcare, and global operations.

In this highly visible leadership role, you will drive the modernization of contract governance, technology, risk management, and service delivery across Cornell University and Weill Cornell Medicine. Partnering with senior leaders and stakeholders across the institution, you will shape enterprise contracting strategy, enhance operational effectiveness, and deliver a best-in-class contracting experience that enables innovation while safeguarding the university's interests.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to influence institutional policy, lead transformative technology initiatives, and establish scalable processes that will create lasting impact across one of the most complex and respected higher education environments in the world.


What You'll Do

Shape Enterprise Contract Strategy and Governance

  • Lead Cornell's enterprise contract management program and long-term strategic vision.
  • Develop and maintain governance frameworks, policies, operating procedures, and service delivery models.
  • Establish and track performance metrics, operational objectives, and key performance indicators.
  • Drive initiatives that increase contracting efficiency, transparency, compliance, and stakeholder satisfaction.
  • Provide executive-level insights and recommendations regarding contract operations, performance, and risk.

Lead Contract Lifecycle Management Technology & Analytics

jobs.description:
What is Reach Financial?

Reach Financial is a FinTech platform helping people outsmart debt for good.

We are building innovative products and best-in-class support that enable our customers to take control of their debt and de-mystify their personal finances. Our products and tools empower our customers to turn their financial goals into a reality.

Reach Financial launched in 2015 and has helped our customers pay off over $1 billion in debt. We offer debt consolidation loans and personal loans; together, these markets represent a $1.5T opportunity. In time, we will expand beyond these products to offer solutions for a variety of our customers' personal finance challenges.

We are a fast-growing and fast-paced FinTech startup with the stability of an established firm. You will have a front-row seat at a rapidly growing company innovating the FinTech industry.

About the role

The Collections Manager leads Team Leads and Operations Specialists and owns day-to-day execution and performance improvement for the assigned collections operation, which may include pre-charge-off, charge-off, or both. The Manager delivers results through effective leadership, workforce management, sound approvals, and consistent operational controls.

Team Leadership and Development

  • Coach and develop Team Leads and Operations Specialists, establish clear objectives, and hold direct reports accountable for results, employee development, and execution.
  • Evaluate Team Lead coaching quality and follow-through. Complete direct-report reviews and calibrate agent evaluations prepared by Team Leads for consistency and accuracy.
  • Oversee formal corrective action and performance improvement plans in partnership with People & Culture, including appropriate documentation and escalation.
  • Lead agent selection within approved hiring plans, partnering with People & Culture and Team Leads on interviews and onboarding readiness.
  • Own onboarding and refresher-training effectiveness. Coordinate delivery with Team Leads and relevant partners, and verify learning through subsequent quality and performance results.

Operations and Workforce Management

  • Own daily operational execution, workload prioritization, scheduling, coverage, PTO, and timecard approvals. Delegate routine monitoring and follow-through to Team Leads.
  • Assess demand, capacity, adherence, and coverage risks. Recommend staffing changes to the Director, who retains ownership of staffing forecasts and headcount decisions.
  • Optimize dialer execution, account prioritization, and targeted outreach within approved parameters. Recommend and evaluate material strategy changes with the Director.
  • Resolve second-level customer and operational escalations, document outcomes, and coordinate root-cause remediation with relevant partners.
  • Maintain accurate procedures and knowledge resources. Obtain required approvals before publishing policy changes and coordinate training and implementation.

Approvals Quality and Compliance

  • Review and approve hardship assistance, forbearance, settlements, and loan modifications within delegated authority. Document decisions and escalate requests outside policy or approval limits.
  • Apply the current approval matrix and transition requirements. Loan-modification authority transfers only after the applicable policy and delegation take effect.
  • Calibrate quality assurance scoring with Team Leads and QA. Monitor adherence to applicable federal and state requirements, approved company policies, and bank partner standards, including TCPA, FDCPA, and Regulation F requirements where applicable.
  • Coordinate with Compliance, QA, and the Director to investigate exceptions, implement corrective actions, and verify remediation. Escalate significant customer, compliance, or operational risks promptly.
  • Oversee inventory and hardship follow-up, complaint handling, and the correct treatment of bankruptcy-related interactions and other accounts requiring restricted or specialized handling.

Performance Analysis and Reporting

  • Own performance improvement for the assigned operation across applicable recovery, delinquency, roll-rate, cure, quality, customer treatment, productivity, and employee development measures.
  • Identify root causes, establish corrective actions with owners and due dates, and measure effectiveness. Evaluate targeted campaigns and approved A/B tests using relevant financial and customer outcomes, including gross and net recoveries where applicable.
  • Validate and consolidate Team Lead reporting, maintain scorecards, and provide the Director with actionable findings, risks, and recommendations. Partner with relevant teams to resolve operational dependencies.
  • Validate commission calculations and supporting data, resolve discrepancies, and submit accurate results to designated recipients within established deadlines.

Required Qualifications

  • At least three years of collections experience, including one year in a supervisory role, with demonstrated ownership of team performance and operational execution.
  • Experience in consumer lending collections relevant to the assigned operation, including appropriate hardship, forbearance, settlement, or loan-modification processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop leaders, evaluate coaching effectiveness, administer corrective action with People & Culture, and maintain employee engagement.
  • Working knowledge of applicable consumer collections requirements, company controls, and sound judgment in applying approval limits and escalating exceptions.
  • Experience using dialer, workforce management, reporting, and customer account systems to prioritize work and improve results.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills, including the ability to identify root causes, manage competing priorities, and drive actions to completion.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing Team Leads or supervisors, leading remote teams, or overseeing both pre-charge-off and charge-off operations.
  • Experience evaluating third-party collection agency performance or designing and assessing collection strategy tests.

What is it like working at Reach Financial?

Our culture is built around advancing our teams, and we are dedicated to the success and growth of every team member. We believe in retaining a high-performing workforce and we prioritize diversity, intellectual curiosity, and continued learning. Our generous benefits packages reflect that.

We’ve been hard at work perfecting our product for years, and now we’re growing faster than ever before. Our strong foundation and company culture is readily equipped for this growth, and we believe that with the right people, our products will continue to help customers make real changes in their financial lives.

What benefits will you receive?

  • Healthcare, Life Insurance, 401k Match
  • Paid Time Off, Paid 12-week Parental Leave
  • Disability (short-term, long-term), Employee Assistance Program
  • Spending Accounts (Transit/Parking, Medical, Dependent Care)
  • Insurance Discounts (home, auto, pet)

Omnis Group is a strategic accounting and advisory firm in Perth, Western Australia, with a 25-year history. We focus on business advisory and growth rather than pure compliance, and we work entirely in the cloud, using automation, AI tools and apps to take manual work out of the process.

We are a fully remote firm. Our Senior Client Manager is in Perth, five team members work from the Philippines and about seven accountants work from India. Working remotely is how the whole firm runs, not an add-on.

Our values: Accountability, Understanding and Collaboration.

Where the role fits

The client managers handle client relationships and advice. You sit between them and the remote team: work comes up through you, reviewed and close to final, and technical questions come down to you. Your team will include senior, intermediate and graduate accountants and bookkeepers in the Philippines and India.

  • Daily team meeting: run the 12:45 pm AWST meeting, set priorities, check progress on every job and clear what is blocking the team.
  • Workflow management: the largest part of the role. Keep Xero Practice Manager current, allocate and schedule jobs, brief the production team in India, follow up missing information and keep work on track against ATO and ASIC deadlines.
  • Pipeline and budget: keep enough work in the system that the team never runs out, and make sure the end-of-month budget is met.
  • Reviews: review your team's work, send back review points and bring jobs to 90 to 100 per-cent complete, completing jobs yourself where needed.
  • Quoting: help the client managers price work by scoping jobs and estimating hours.
  • Training: coach your team in financial statements, tax returns, bookkeeping and payroll, and keep checklists and procedures up to date.
  • Questions: answer technical questions from the team and client managers, and handle written client queries on bookkeeping and individual tax returns.
  • Client meetings: occasionally join the Senior Client Manager in online meetings on tax planning, structuring, software or business mentoring.

What you will need

  • Strong knowledge of Division 7A, CGT and the small business concessions, trust distributions, franking, depreciation, non-commercial losses, superannuation guarantee, FBT and payroll tax.
  • Experience leading and motivating a remote team, and holding them to budget and deadline.
  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to explain technical issues simply and give clear, direct feedback.
  • Calm and organised across competing deadlines and takes ownership without being asked.

Software

Xero and Xero Practice Manager, Class and BGL, NowInfinity, FYI Docs, MYOB, Hubdoc, Microsoft 365, ATO Tax Agent Portal, ChangeGPS, Ignition, Loom and Time Doctor.

What we offer

  • Permanent, full-time work from home with flexible start and finish times
  • All equipment supplied
  • A day off for your birthday
  • Monthly one-to-one reviews with the Client Manager
  • Support for tax and technology training

You will need a reliable internet connection and a quiet place to work from home.

How we recruit

Shortlisted candidates complete a skills test on Australian accounting and tax, a personality assessment, an interview with the Client Manager and reference checks with previous Australian employers.

The Role:

11:11 is seeking a Product Manager to lead the product organization’s role in our public cloud and strategic vendor ecosystem. This role is responsible for cloud billing analysis, billing escalation support, vendor commercial and licensing coordination, product interoperability, and the translation of provider and partner requirements into scalable product and operational processes across 11:11’s managed public cloud services. The position has a strong focus on AWS and Azure while remaining broad enough to support other strategic vendors whose commercial models, licensing structures, support changes, or interoperability requirements affect the business.

This role also supports the ongoing definition and evolution of 11:11’s managed public cloud services for customers who rely on 11:11 to operate and support public cloud environments. Working closely with Finance, Procurement, Billing, Engineering, Service Delivery, Operations, Connectivity, Sales, Marketing, and customer-facing teams, this leader will drive service definition, commercial alignment, operational readiness, and roadmap inputs that improve how cloud- and vendor-related capabilities are packaged, supported, billed, and delivered.

The ideal candidate brings strong product leadership, deep familiarity with public cloud billing and vendor commercial constructs, and the ability to translate complex provider and partner requirements into scalable product and operational outcomes.

This is a full-time, remote role, based in the United States, reporting to the VP, Product Management.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the product organization’s participation in cloud financial operations, including analysis and reconciliation of usage, discounts, credits, support charges, and billing exceptions across provider data, internal billing systems, and customer-facing outputs
  • Partner with Finance, Procurement, Billing, Connectivity, and strategic vendors to improve forecasting, purchasing, invoicing, escalation handling, credit reconciliation, reporting, and overall billing accuracy while reducing manual exceptions and process friction
  • Serve as a subject matter expert on cloud commercial constructs, payer-account implications, vendor licensing mechanics, committed-consumption frameworks, and the ways these elements affect product, interoperability, reporting, and monetization
  • Represent product interests in relationships with AWS, Azure, and other strategic vendors where commercial terms, support changes, account structures, licensing models, or technical interoperability affect customer experience or revenue realization
  • Define and evolve 11:11’s managed public cloud services, including service scope, support boundaries, commercial alignment, packaging, and fit within the broader product and services portfolio
  • Partner with Engineering, Service Delivery, Service Operations, Connectivity, and adjacent business teams to translate cloud and vendor requirements into product requirements, backlog items, roadmap priorities, policy and process improvements, documentation, and operationally ready service workflows
  • Work supportively with colleagues, operating in a manner that is consistent with 11:11’s Code of Business Ethics and Company Values
  • Responsibly receive, transmit, and handle company data and information per Company data handling agreements, work procedures and policies
  • Review and follow company policies and guidelines, data privacy practices, including annual compliance training certification and policy acknowledgements
  • Additional duties as assigned

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent years of related work experience required
  • 5+ years of experience as a Product Manager or in a similar role within cloud, managed services, infrastructure, or technology services environments
  • Deep knowledge of public cloud billing mechanisms and terminology, especially AWS, with familiarity across Azure billing, account structures, support models, commercial constructs, and cloud commerce frameworks
  • Experience analyzing cloud usage, discounts, credits, support charges, billing exceptions, and related reporting or forecasting needs across provider data, internal systems, and customer-facing outputs
  • Strong understanding of how commercial, support, licensing, and interoperability requirements affect product packaging, monetization, operational workflows, and customer experience
  • Demonstrated ability to define product requirements, manage backlogs, and translate complex provider and partner requirements into scalable product capabilities, process improvements, and roadmap priorities
  • Strong cross-functional leadership, analytical problem-solving, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to drive coordinated outcomes across Finance, Procurement, Billing Operations, Engineering, Service Delivery, Operations, Connectivity, Sales, and customer-facing teams
  • Strong communication skills and customer orientation with the ability to explain complex billing, licensing, and service concepts to technical and non-technical audiences while maintaining focus on operational clarity, billing accuracy, and measurable business outcomes
  • Understanding of managed services concepts, including service scope definition, support boundaries, operational readiness, and delivering resilient, supportable services at scale preferred
  • Experience with service provider or MSP business models, including recurring revenue, service packaging, attach strategies, and cross-functional operating models preferred
  • Familiarity with metering, billing, usage reporting, customer-facing portals or consoles, and related integrations in cloud or managed service environments
  • Experience working with AWS, Azure, and strategic technology vendors in environments where commercial and operational changes must be translated into repeatable internal processes
  • Familiarity with AWS Marketplace commercial constructs, private offers, billing flows, and related go-to-market or operational considerations preferred
  • Occasional travel to 11:11 locations, data centers, customer sites, or industry events may be required

The Brand Manager leads the positioning, commercialization, and go-to-market strategy for a portfolio of Ritual products. This role owns how assigned products are brought to market and communicated to consumers across DTC, Amazon, and Retail.

The Brand Manager independently leads defined product and commercialization initiatives, translating consumer, product, and business insights into clear marketing strategies and compelling consumer storytelling. This person serves as a cross-functional partner across Innovation, Science, Regulatory, Creative, Growth, and Customer, proactively identifying opportunities, navigating tradeoffs, and driving work forward within their scope.

What you'll do

  • Lead end-to-end product commercialization and go-to-market strategy for assigned products and key initiatives, developing positioning, messaging, launch plans, and integrated marketing strategies from concept through execution.
  • Develop clear, differentiated product positioning and messaging, independently translating product features, scientific information, consumer insights, and competitive trends into compelling consumer-facing stories.
  • Serve as the cross-functional marketing lead for assigned launches and commercialization initiatives, building strong partnerships and driving alignment across Product Innovation, Science, Regulatory, Creative, Growth, Customer, Retail, Sales, and other key stakeholders.
  • Develop and execute integrated launch and marketing plans in partnership with channel teams, proactively identifying dependencies, risks, and tradeoffs and bringing forward recommendations to keep initiatives moving. Ensure current portfolio health is checked and tracking towards goals.
  • Lead ongoing product messaging and creative optimization, using consumer insights, competitive trends, and performance data to identify opportunities, test new approaches, and improve product adoption, conversion, and engagement.
  • Monitor and analyze product and campaign performance, synthesizing multiple sources of business, consumer, and market data into clear insights, recommendations, and actions.
  • Partner with Consumer Insights and Product Innovation to understand consumer needs, category trends, and whitespace opportunities, helping inform product positioning, innovation, and future commercialization strategies.
  • Manage key elements of the product lifecycle, including expansions, reformulations, packaging updates, claims changes, and other initiatives, while proactively identifying gaps and opportunities that improve the consumer experience and product performance.

Who you are

  • A creative problem solver. You independently work through routine challenges and bottlenecks, and when facing a new or more complex problem, you bring forward thoughtful options and recommendations—not just questions.
  • Strategic and curious. You are naturally curious and dig deep to understand consumers, products, categories, and business performance. You can quickly absorb new information and adapt your approach when priorities or strategies shift.
  • A dot connector. You look beyond your immediate work to understand dependencies, tradeoffs, and opportunities across teams. You proactively identify potential gaps and help connect the right people and information to move work forward.
  • A sound decision maker. You use multiple inputs—including data, consumer insights, stakeholder perspectives, and judgment—to make thoughtful decisions and clearly articulate your rationale.
  • A strong collaborator. You build productive relationships across functions, proactively share information, and adapt your working style to complement the strengths and expertise of others.
  • A clear and kind communicator. You communicate clearly and thoughtfully, tailoring your message and communication style to the audience and creating alignment around priorities, decisions, and next steps.
  • An agile learner. You embrace new information, approaches, and ways of working. You adapt quickly to changing priorities, identify potential friction early, and view change as an opportunity to improve.
  • Accountable for the outcome. You take ownership of your work from start to finish, maintain a high bar for quality, proactively communicate risks or timeline changes, and use the appropriate tools and support to keep projects moving.

What you'll need

  • Education: BS/BA, preferably in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field. Equivalent experience also accepted.
  • Experience: 4+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Brand Management, Marketing, or a related role, preferably within CPG, VMS, wellness, beauty, or another consumer-focused industry.
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading product launches, commercialization initiatives, or complex marketing workstreams from strategy through execution.
  • Strong experience developing product positioning, messaging, and consumer-facing marketing, with the ability to translate complex product information into clear and compelling storytelling.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to independently resolve routine challenges and bring thoughtful options and recommendations to leadership when navigating more complex or ambiguous decisions.
  • Ability to synthesize multiple sources of consumer, market, and business data to identify opportunities, understand tradeoffs, and recommend clear paths forward.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and project management skills, with strong accountability for deliverable quality, timelines, and project outcomes.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to build relationships, proactively connect workstreams, and drive alignment across multiple stakeholders.

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification listed above. We're committed to building a diverse team and recognize that skills can be developed in many different ways.

Compensation

  • Pay Range: $106,000 - $140,000
  • Your base salary is one part of your total compensation package. The salary range represents the entire compensation range for this position. Exact compensation will depend on a number of factors, which may include the successful candidate's skills, level, years of experience, technical expertise, and other qualifications. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. This role is also eligible for equity + generous benefits + 401k + unlimited PTO etc - see our list of perks/ benefits below.

Req Title - Workday Delivery & Methods Lead - Accenture Edge

Which Market Unit / Marketwide - Marketwide

Management Level –

We Are:

The Accenture Edge Workday Mid-market business is a core growth driver within Accenture, focused on helping Mid-market companies reinvent, scale, and compete with the agility required in today’s market. Mid-market organizations share the same bold ambitions as large enterprises, they are undergoing a significant transformation, driven by the need to modernize operations, accelerate growth, and respond to evolving industry demands. Accenture brings the full strength of our global capabilities—deep industry expertise, ecosystem partnerships, and proven innovation—to make enterprise grade solutions accessible, scalable, and simplified for midmarket needs. Powered by curated offerings, preconfigured solutions, accelerators, and AI enabled delivery models, Accenture Mid-market brings together teams across our global network to help clients drive real ROI, innovate faster, and transform with confidence. The Mid-market portfolio spans repeatable, industrialized solutions across technology, operations, security, cloud, and industry-specific needs to meet clients where they are on their reinvention journey.

We are looking to expand our Workday Edge Mid-market team with the best talent, who have experience in the mid-market, across the business suite, and across functions, that will enable us to continue to drive transformations at scale.

You Are:

You are an experienced delivery leader who is comfortable owning complex Workday programs end to end, managing budgets, risks and governance, and building trust with client executives. You bring the core capabilities of a Workday Delivery Lead across Financials, HCM or full-platform (Financials and HCM) programs, along with the judgment to shape how delivery is done: defining repeatable approaches, tools and contract language that help mid-market engagements start fast and run consistently.

The Work:

As the Methods Lead, you will evolve the delivery management approach for Edge Workday engagements in the mid-market. You will solidify mid-market delivery approaches and tooling, incorporate AI-enabled delivery into how engagements are run, own the SOW language for delivery methods and supporting materials, apply lessons learned from active engagements to improve the methods, and support the growth of the delivery portfolio. You will be responsible for client success and the referenceability of the projects you lead.

As the Delivery Lead, you will team with mid-market clients on their Workday transformation programs through your combined mid-market and Workday delivery expertise, which includes your ability to:

· Lead day-to-day delivery of Workday Financials, HCM or full-platform programs for mid-market clients across solution design, budget management, resource planning and quality assurance

· Serve as the primary escalation point for delivery issues, proactively identifying risks and implementing mitigation strategies

· Partner with client stakeholders to align on scope, timelines and deliverable expectations throughout the project lifecycle

· Manage onshore/offshore delivery team structures, coordinating across time zones for seamless execution and knowledge transfer

· Drive cutover planning, rehearsals and execution, ensuring a controlled and successful transition to the live Workday environment

· Oversee project financials, including EAC, revenue recognition, margin management and change order processing

· Facilitate governance rituals, including steering committee meetings, project status reporting and executive briefings

· Ensure adherence to Accenture delivery standards, quality frameworks and client contractual obligations

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements


What You Need:

  • Active Workday Pro certification in Financials (such as Record to Report) or HCM (such as HCM Core)
  • A minimum of 12 years of experience in enterprise technology delivery or project leadership, including at least 5 years of hands-on Workday functional experience in Financials and/or HCM
  • A minimum of 3 full-lifecycle Workday implementations managed end to end, from initiation through go-live and hypercare, with accountability for scope, schedule and delivery quality across teams of 5+ resources
  • A minimum of 3 years leading offshore or distributed delivery teams of 5+ resources across 2+ time zones
  • A minimum of 3 years of executive-level stakeholder engagement, including steering committee presentations, escalation management and status reporting to VP-level or C-suite audiences
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent (12 years) work experience (If an Associate’s Degree, 6 years of work experience)

Bonus Points If:

  • Experience delivering Workday solutions for mid-market clients (revenues of about $300M to $3B) and familiarity with their constraints and compressed timelines
  • Experience delivering both Workday Financials and HCM, including full-platform programs
  • Active PMP (Project Management Professional) certification from PMI
  • A minimum of 2 go-live cutovers managed, including cutover runbooks, mock cutovers and go/no-go decisions
  • A minimum of 3 years managing project financials, resource plans and delivery risk across 3+ simultaneous workstreams
  • Familiarity with Workday deployment methodology and agile delivery practices
  • Experience developing delivery methodologies, accelerators, SOW templates or delivery tooling

About Accenture

Accenture is a leading global professional services company that helps the world’s leading businesses, governments and other organizations build their digital core, optimize their operations, accelerate revenue growth and enhance citizen services—creating tangible value at speed and scale. Technology is at the core of change today, and we are one of the world’s leaders in helping drive that change, with strong ecosystem relationships. We combine our strength in technology and leadership in cloud, data and AI with unmatched industry experience, functional expertise and global delivery capability. Our broad range of services, solutions and assets across Strategy & Consulting, Technology, Operations, Industry X and Song, together with our culture of shared success and commitment to creating 360° value, enable us to help our clients reinvent and build trusted, lasting relationships. jobs.description:
About The Job
Title: Client Success Manager
Department: Client Services
Location: Remote
Employment Type: Full Time
Reports To: Client Success Team Lead - Accelerator Business Unit
Who We Are
Clever Digital Marketing (CDM) is a performance marketing agency trusted by the largest home improvement companies across North America. We specialize in scaling client growth through full-funnel paid media strategies and deep business consulting. CDM’s success is powered by its industry-leading reputation for exceptional service delivery and performance, with growth driven almost entirely by client referrals and expansion.
Our Accelerator Business Unit partners with fast-growing home improvement companies investing from $15K–$100K/month in paid media. These clients rely on us for more than advertising—they look to us as advisors on their sales process, lead quality, speed-to-lead, operational alignment, and long-term profitability.
Our agency thrives on ownership, proactive leadership, high performance, and results. We move fast, think strategically, and operate with a builder’s mindset. If that excites you, you’ll feel right at home.
The Opportunity
We’re hiring a Client Success Manager to own and grow a mid-market portfolio within our Accelerator unit. You’ll manage 10–15 accounts (or ~$650K in managed ad spend), serving as the primary point of contact and strategic partner for home improvement companies across North America. ￼
This role sits at the intersection of performance insight, client communication & relationship leadership, business consultation, and proactive problem-solving. You’ll break down performance data, diagnose funnel issues, and communicate recommendations with clarity and confidence—and you’ll do it while managing relationships built on trust, accountability, and honest partnership.
This role is perfect for someone who is analytical, proactive, and strong with people. The candidate should be comfortable breaking down performance data, diagnosing funnel issues, and communicating clearly with clients from different backgrounds and experience levels.
You’ll work closely with senior media buyers, internal leadership, and cross-functional teams to drive performance, retention, and client satisfaction.
Your north star metric: Client Lifetime Value, driven through proactive communication, retention, and consistent value delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Client Relationship Management
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for your portfolio, building trust through proactive communication and consistency.
  • Respond promptly to client questions, simplifying complex topics and ensuring alignment and clarity on next steps.
  • Guide clients through challenges with confidence, empathy, and a solution-oriented approach.
  • Demonstrate strong client management presence: calm, composed, clear, even in fast-paced, high-pressure moments.
Performance Insight & Reviews
  • Analyze Facebook and Google campaign performance across the funnel from lead generation through SQL (Sales Qualified Leads) and revenue indicators.
  • Diagnose bottlenecks, identify trends, and translate complex data into simple, actionable insights.
  • Present performance reviews that drive clarity, direction, and next steps￼.
Strategic Consultation
  • Lead bi-weekly client calls focused on performance reviews and strategic alignment while ensuring every call delivers clarity, direction, and meaningful next steps.
  • Advise clients on operational improvements that impact lead quality, speed-to-lead, sales cadence, and conversion performance.
  • Tailor guidance to each client’s goals, growth stage, and unique challenges.
Growth and Retention
  • Maintain strong portfolio retention by delivering consistent value and anticipating risks early.
  • Identify upsell and cross-channel opportunities in collaboration with Senior CSMs and Team Lead.
  • Anticipate and champion scalable client growth through proactive thinking and ideation, improving the client experience, and positioning the agency as a true strategic partner.
Internal Collaboration
  • Partner with Meta and PPC media buyers to align on insights, opportunities, and challenges.
  • Support cross-department communication to ensure smooth execution and timely updates.
  • Escalate challenges quickly and constructively, contributing clarity and structure rather than noise.
  • Embody a builder’s mindset, creating tools, resources, and frameworks that improve how we deliver.
Professional Development & Contribution
  • Stay current on paid media best practices, industry trends, and home improvement nuances.
  • Participate in ongoing CSM training sessions, process improvements, and department-wide initiatives.
  • Contribute ideas, templates, and frameworks that elevate team efficiency, client experience, and operational rigor. ￼

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

Who You Are
You’re a strong communicator with analytical depth. You connect the dots between performance data, funnel performance, and business outcomes—and explain them simply and succinctly. You take ownership, anticipate needs, and bring clarity to both clients and internal teams. You are grounded, curious, and comfortable managing competing priorities with composure. You’re:
  • Clear & concise: You simplify complex performance insights into actionable takeaways.
  • Analytical: You’re comfortable navigating data across multiple platforms and spotting what matters.
  • Empathetic but direct: You build trust by communicating with honesty, tact, and client-first intention.
  • Proactive: You use your curiosity and expertise to identify risks and opportunities before others see them, acting with intent without waiting to be told.
  • Process-driven & organized: You manage multiple accounts with detail-oriented execution.
  • Calm under pressure: You bring composure, clarity, and presence to fast-paced environments.
  • Growth-minded & coachable: You see feedback as fuel.
  • Solution-focused: You default to ownership, not excuses, and you solve problems before they become blockers.
  • Relationship-oriented: You build client rapport and trust through strong people skills, honest communication, curiosity, and follow-through.
Qualifications
Required
  • 4+ years in a client-facing, portfolio management, or account management role.
  • Strong soft skills: communication, clarity, client rapport, and expectation-setting.
  • High proficiency with Excel/Sheets and performance dashboards.
  • Experience analyzing marketing or sales funnels, even if not in paid media.
  • Ability to manage a portfolio of 10–15 accounts and maintain strong retention.
Preferred
  • Performance marketing or digital agency experience
    and/or experience working within an internal marketing team at a home services company.
  • Familiarity with Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, and Looker Studio.
  • Experience in home improvement, home services, or high-ticket lead generation.
  • Strong understanding of B2C or high-ticket service funnels.
  • Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, or related fields.

Benefits

Benefits of Working at CDM
  • Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses
  • Flexible remote work environment with option for in-person collaboration (Vaughan, ON)
  • Group Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision, RRSP/401k Plan w/matching, more.
  • Company-provided MacBook computer
  • Home office budget and Clever merch delivery to get you started
  • Work Abroad Policy: Need a new working environment? Our work abroad policy supports this!
  • The chance to shape and grow a high-performing Client Success team
  • A culture of performance and respect where the best work happens with extreme ownership and accountability meets collaboration.
  • We promote from within! There's a clear internal growth path to an Account Director role, with the opportunity to take on larger budgets and more complex client accounts.

Clever Digital Marketing values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the team. We are happy to provide reasonable accommodations to candidates in need of support during the recruitment and selection process. Please note that artificial intelligence (AI) may be utilized during the interview or candidate evaluation process to support the fair and efficient screening, assessment, and selection of applicants.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Human Appeal is a global non-profit humanitarian and development organisation. We deliver life-saving emergency assistance such as food, medical aid, and disaster relief. At the same time, we run sustainable, community-led programmes in healthcare, education, and livelihoods to build resilience and self-reliance. Our experienced local teams work in vulnerable, hard-to-reach areas. Guided by a vision of a just, caring, and sustainable world, our mission is to save lives, alleviate poverty, and empower communities in line with the core humanitarian principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, and independence.

Position Overview

The Fundraising Coordinator supports the planning, coordination and delivery of Human Appeal Canada’s regional fundraising campaigns, events and community partnerships. The role builds relationships with donors, mosques, community organizations and volunteers to raise awareness of Human Appeal’s humanitarian work and achieve agreed fundraising targets.

Working closely with the fundraising team, the Coordinator identifies new opportunities, delivers well-organized activities and maintains accurate donor and income records. The role contributes to year-over-year growth in donations and donor engagement while ensuring responsible use of resources, a positive donor experience and compliance with organizational policies.

Please note this role will be posted on an ongoing rolling basis and AI will be used in sourcing candidates. This is also a new role.

The salary range for this role is $63,750-$75,000

Main Responsibilities

Campaign and event coordination

  • Coordinate regional fundraising activities, including community appeals, fundraising dinners, exhibitions, conferences and seasonal campaigns such as Ramadan.
  • Prepare activity plans, timelines, logistics and resource requirements in line with the approved regional fundraising plan.
  • Support emergency appeals and adapt activities to emerging humanitarian needs and local community opportunities.
  • Work toward agreed individual and regional income, donor-growth and engagement targets, with appropriate return on investment.
  • Monitor campaign results and expenditure against approved budgets; provide timely progress updates, flag risks and recommend improvements.
  • Contribute practical ideas and community insights to regional fundraising plans and post-event reviews.

Donor and community relationships

  • Develop and maintain relationships with donors, mosques, community groups, businesses and other local partners.
  • Act as a regional contact for assigned partners, coordinate follow-up and support partnership discussions within delegated authority.
  • Share accurate information about Human Appeal’s projects and impact; respond professionally to inquiries and refer complaints through the appropriate channels.

Team and volunteer coordination

  • Coordinate volunteer briefings, schedules and event-day tasks, ensuring volunteers understand their responsibilities and safeguarding expectations.
  • Work with fundraising, marketing, finance and other colleagues to arrange approved materials, consistent messaging and smooth campaign delivery.
  • Participate in team meetings and support colleagues during peak fundraising periods and national campaigns.

Administration and financial controls

  • Maintain accurate, timely and confidential donor, partner, activity and income records in approved systems.
  • Follow cash-handling procedures, including counting, logging, securing, sealing, labeling and depositing funds; reconcile collections with Finance.
  • Maintain supporting records for income and expenditure, and promptly report discrepancies, missing documentation or control concerns.

Compliance and professional standards

  • Follow Human Appeal Canada’s fundraising, safeguarding, privacy, health and safety, financial-control and conduct policies, together with applicable Canadian requirements.
  • Use approved fundraising messages and materials, respect donor preferences and protect confidential information.
  • Participate in relevant training and professional development, and undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role.

NB:Employee duties are not limited only to the above-mentioned responsibilities; they may perform other duties as assigned

Authority and working relationships

Deliver assigned activities within approved plans and delegated authority. Expenditure must remain within approved budgets and authorization limits. Escalate contractual commitments and decisions outside delegated authority to the reporting manager. This role has no direct reports; volunteer coordination does not imply hiring, promotion or formal supervisory authority.

Interna working relationships l: Fundraising, Finance, Marketing and Communications, volunteer support, People and Culture, and relevant program colleagues. External relationships: Donors, mosque and community leaders, volunteers, corporate and community partners, venues and suppliers.

Candidate essential criteria

  • Degree in a related field.
  • At least two years of relevant experience in fundraising, community engagement, or project and event coordination.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate activities, manage competing deadlines and build productive stakeholder relationships.
  • Strong planning, organization and follow-through, with attention to detail and accurate recordkeeping.
  • Clear written and verbal communication in English, with confident presentation and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues, donors, community partners and volunteers.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and competence using social media to support outreach and fundraising.
  • Ability to track budgets, income and activity results, and follow financial and cash-handling procedures.
  • Sound judgment, discretion and commitment to donor confidentiality, safeguarding and ethical fundraising.
  • Flexibility to support regional activities and peak fundraising periods.

Candidate desirable criteria

  • Experience using donor management or customer relationship management systems, such as Salesforce.
  • Experience in a charity or humanitarian organization, including mosque-based or community fundraising.
  • Additional language skills, such as French, Arabic or Urdu.

How to apply

We are keen to appoint the right person for this position as soon as possible and will be considering applications as they are received. To maximize your opportunity, please submit your CV by clicking the link provided to apply. We look forward to receiving your application and hearing from you.

Please note that we will only be contacting the shortlisted candidates. Applying candidates must have the legal authorisation or right to work in the designated work location/duty station.

Disclaimer: Human Appeal is committed to diversity, social inclusion, and gender equality/balance, and strongly encourages applications from underrepresented groups. The organisation maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH), with all staff required to comply with Preventing Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (PSEA/SH) standards and safe recruitment procedures.

Salary: $63,750-$75,000

We also provide payment solutions such as FedNow Instant Payment Xchange™ (IPX), Skip-A-Pay, and Quick Pay. Over 100 customers trust Tyfone's solutions, which are supported by over 200 integrations and over 140 patents. Tyfone has been recognized as a Best Place to Work in Fintech by American Banker and has received multiple awards for its solutions. The company operates with a lean-team model for external engagements to manage costs, increase selling time, and accelerate pipeline velocity. Tyfone values collaborative execution as the path to market leadership.

We are an equal-opportunity employer, and we encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

Role overview

The Technical Customer Success Manager is a forward deployed engineer who owns the technical health of every customer's Tyfone solution, from configuration and go-live through ongoing support. You will understand the nFinia platform at code level, engage customers directly on technical requirements, lead a team of configuration engineers who work in Yogi, support customer go-lives on-site, and use AI agents that read incoming tickets, fix the code, and deploy the fix with light human oversight.

Key responsibilities

Technical customer engagement

  • Act as the technical voice of Tyfone with customer IT, security and operations teams, translating business needs into configuration and integration requirements.

  • Lead technical discovery and solution walkthroughs, and document decisions so the build, definition and discovery stay aligned.

  • Join client on-sites as a hands-on engineer, not only as a presenter.

Solution configuration

  • Configure nFinia and related products (Loanovia, Payfinia, Nuuvia) from each customer's needs using Yogi, and own configuration correctness across environments.

  • Validate integrations with cores, processors and third-party partners before go-live and after each release.

  • Maintain configuration standards, templates and checklists so setups are repeatable across clients.

Go-lives and on-site delivery

  • Support customer go-lives end to end: readiness checks, cutover planning, hypercare and handoff to Support.

  • Be on-site at the customer during critical go-live windows, working alongside the customer's technical team and resolving issues in real time.

  • Own the technical go-live criteria and sign off that configuration, integrations and data are ready before launch.

Team leadership and Yogi mastery

  • Manage a team of configuration engineers who build and maintain customer configurations in Yogi: set priorities, review their work and coach them.

  • Become the in-house expert on Yogi, including its configuration model, diagrams and instrumentation, and drive its roadmap with the teams that build it.

  • Set configuration quality standards and review practices so every customer setup is consistent and traceable.

  • Lead and mentor the team's engineers, including recruiting, performance evaluations and continuous improvement of how the team works.

  • Report customer satisfaction and team performance metrics to leadership, and coordinate staffing and resources with Engineering and DevOps.

  • Hold periodic customer meetings to review health, open issues and upcoming work.

Self-healing agents

  • Work with engineering and internal teams to design, build and deploy AI agents that analyze incoming tickets, locate the root cause in the code base, implement the fix and deploy it automatically.

  • Define which ticket classes are safe for full automation and which need human approval, and tune the agents against real ticket data.

  • Build guardrails: test generation, staged rollout, rollback paths and an audit trail for every automated change.

Oversight and QA

  • Review agent-proposed fixes, run QA on high-risk changes, and own the manual oversight loop until the agents earn more autonomy.

  • Track agent accuracy, fix success rate and regressions, and report them to leadership each month.

  • Feed recurring issues back to Engineering and Product as root-cause fixes, not repeated patches.

Support, incidents and escalations

  • Triage, prioritize and resolve customer issues, troubleshooting production applications and infrastructure alongside developers and DevOps.

  • Collect and analyze logs, and escalate complex issues to Engineering with clear reproduction steps and context.

  • Manage client escalations and critical incidents end to end, and communicate status to credit union and bank customers throughout.

  • Take part in the on-call rotation for critical incidents.

Program and delivery discipline

The role pairs engineering depth with the planning rigor expected of a strong program manager.

  • Own the technical plan for each assigned customer: scope, milestones, dependencies, risks and owners, tracked in Jira with dates and sprint visibility.

  • Run regular technical status reviews with customers and internal teams, and escalate risks early with a clear mitigation and decision needed.

  • Manage scope against the signed statement of work, and flag change requests with effort and impact before work starts.

  • Coordinate across Delivery, Support, Engineering and DevOps so handoffs have a named owner and a due date.

  • Publish concise status reports and post-go-live reviews covering open issues, ticket trends and lessons learned.

  • Operate with stakeholder communication discipline: single source of truth, written follow-ups after every customer call, and no dates held only in spreadsheets.

Required qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • 6+ years in forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, technical customer success, implementation or delivery roles for a SaaS or fintech product.

  • Strong coding ability and comfort reading and changing a production code base, plus working knowledge of APIs, integrations, databases and cloud deployment.

  • Hands-on experience with LLMs and agent tooling: prompt design, tool use, code-aware agents, evaluation and guardrails.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing and safe release practices (staged rollout, rollback).

  • Working knowledge of microservices architecture, cloud troubleshooting and log analysis tools such as Splunk or ELK.

  • Proven ability to run technical conversations with customer engineers and executives and turn requirements into working configuration.

  • 3+ years leading a team of configuration, implementation or application support engineers on complex hosted applications, with the ability to reach mastery of a proprietary configuration tool such as Yogi.

  • Experience supporting go-lives, including on-site cutovers and hypercare at customer locations.

  • Incident management experience, including handling client escalations and critical incidents with customer-facing leadership.

  • Experience managing multiple customer programs with Jira and Confluence, including scope, risk and dependency tracking.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with comfort collaborating with distributed engineering, delivery and support teams across time zones.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with digital banking, core banking integrations, payments (ACH, instant payments) or other regulated financial services.

  • Prior work with credit unions or community banks, and familiarity with security, compliance and audit expectations in banking.

  • Experience building or operating automated ticket triage, auto-remediation or AIOps systems.

  • Program or project management credenti

jobs.description:
Head of Change Management – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Head of Change Management is responsible for developing, leading, and implementing the organization's change management framework to support business transformation, organizational development, digital adoption, and operational improvement initiatives.

Within the Insurance & Investments sector, the role manages organizational change activities associated with technology implementation, business process redesign, operating model changes, regulatory initiatives, restructuring, and cultural transformation.

The incumbent works closely with executive leadership, HR, IT, business unit heads, and programme management teams to assess organizational impacts, improve change readiness, manage resistance, and ensure employees successfully adopt new systems, processes, and ways of working.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Change Management Strategy & Planning

  • Develop and implement the organization's change management strategy, frameworks, and methodologies.
  • Translate transformation objectives into structured change management plans and implementation roadmaps.
  • Establish change management standards, governance structures, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Assess organizational readiness and identify potential challenges associated with planned changes.
  • Align change management activities with corporate strategy and transformation priorities.

B. Organizational Change & Transformation

  • Lead change initiatives involving organizational restructuring, operating model redesign, business process improvement, and operational transformation.
  • Conduct change impact assessments to identify effects on employees, departments, workflows, and systems.
  • Develop implementation plans to support smooth transitions across business functions.
  • Coordinate change activities across multiple projects and transformation programmes.
  • Ensure new organizational structures, processes, and procedures are effectively adopted.

C. Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

  • Identify key stakeholders and develop appropriate engagement strategies.
  • Collaborate with senior management, department heads, employees, and external partners.
  • Develop and deliver change communication plans, presentations, and employee engagement initiatives.
  • Address employee concerns, manage resistance, and build commitment to transformation initiatives.
  • Establish feedback channels to monitor stakeholder sentiment and change effectiveness.

D. Digital & Technology Change Adoption

  • Lead change management activities related to digital transformation and technology implementation.
  • Support the adoption of enterprise systems, automation platforms, digital tools, and business applications.
  • Coordinate with IT teams to assess the organizational impact of technology changes.
  • Develop employee training, awareness, and user adoption programmes.
  • Monitor system adoption and ensure successful transition to new digital working practices.

E. People, Culture & Capability Development

  • Partner with HR to align change initiatives with workforce planning and organizational development.
  • Lead initiatives to improve organizational culture, employee engagement, and leadership alignment.
  • Identify employee capability gaps and coordinate training and development activities.
  • Support managers in leading teams through organizational transitions.
  • Promote adaptability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

F. Change Impact, Risk & Readiness Management

  • Conduct organizational change impact assessments and readiness evaluations.
  • Identify risks, resistance points, and implementation challenges.
  • Develop mitigation plans to minimize disruption to business operations.
  • Monitor change readiness, employee adoption, and implementation effectiveness.
  • Ensure change initiatives comply with applicable insurance, investment, financial services, and regulatory requirements.

G. Performance Monitoring & Benefits Realization

  • Establish change management KPIs, adoption metrics, and performance dashboards.
  • Track employee engagement, training completion, stakeholder readiness, and adoption rates.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of change management activities.
  • Monitor whether transformation initiatives achieve their intended business outcomes.
  • Prepare progress reports and recommendations for senior management and programme steering committees.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Organizational Psychology, Management, or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree or MBA in Business Administration, Organizational Development, or Change Management is preferred.
  • 10–15+ years of progressive experience in change management, organizational development, business transformation, or programme management.
  • At least 5 years in a senior change management or organizational transformation leadership role.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-wide or business-unit change initiatives.
  • Experience in insurance, banking, investment management, or financial services is highly desirable.
  • Strong knowledge of change management frameworks, stakeholder engagement, change impact assessment, and organizational readiness.
  • Experience supporting digital transformation, technology adoption, business process redesign, and organizational restructuring.
  • Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Certifications such as Prosci Change Management, CCMP, APMG Change Management, or equivalent are advantageous.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Successful implementation of the organization's change management strategy.
  • Employee adoption and engagement rates across transformation initiatives.
  • Organizational readiness and change acceptance scores.
  • Completion rates of employee training and capability development programmes.
  • Effectiveness of stakeholder communication and engagement.
  • Reduction in resistance-related delays and implementation risks.
  • Successful adoption of new systems, processes, and operating models.
  • Achievement of transformation objectives and expected business benefits.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and management feedback.
  • Compliance with change management governance and reporting standards.

Led by our talented teams around the world, Cubic is committed to solving global issues through innovation and service to our customers and partners.

We have a top-tier portfolio of businesses, including Cubic Transportation Systems (CTS) and Cubic Defense (CD). Explore more on Cubic.com.

Job Details:

Senior Obsolescence Engineer – (LVC Systems) Eng


Job Summary:

The Senior Obsolescence Engineer is responsible for developing and executing a proactive, data-driven approach to identify, assess, and mitigate components, subsystem, and system-level obsolescence across Cubic’s LVC Ground product suite.

This role supports the long-term sustainability, supportability, and modernization of complex integrated systems by evaluating lifecycle risks and developing technically sound, cost-effective mitigation strategies.

The Senior Obsolescence Engineer works closely with the Chief Engineer, Engineering Leadership, Product Management, and Supply Chain to assess obsolescence risks, evaluate system-level impacts, and develop phased product refresh recommendations aligned to 1–3 year, 3–5 year, and 5+ year planning horizons.

The successful candidate will possess a strong systems engineering mindset and be capable of evaluating obsolescence beyond individual components, including the potential impacts of changes on system architecture, interfaces, requirements, software, integration, verification, supportability, and overall product lifecycle.

This role will promote the use of commercially available, off-the-shelf (COTS) solutions where appropriate to reduce long-term risk, lifecycle cost, and vendor dependency while supporting future product evolution.


Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement a standardized obsolescence management approach across the LVC Ground product portfolio.
  • Leverage automated and AI-enabled obsolescence management tools and commercial data services to perform DMSMS monitoring and analysis, including BOM analysis, component lifecycle tracking, EOL/NRND identification, supplier and supply-chain risk monitoring, lifecycle alerts, and identification of potential alternate components.
  • Identify and assess component, subsystem, and system lifecycle risks, including end-of-life (EOL), diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortages (DMSMS), supplier constraints, single-source dependencies, and aging technologies.
  • Build and maintain product-level obsolescence roadmaps across 1–3 year, 3–5 year, and 5+ year planning horizons.
  • Assess the system-level impact of obsolescence issues, including potential effects on system architecture, interfaces, requirements, hardware, software, integration, verification, configuration, and product supportability.
  • Develop and recommend mitigation strategies including alternate components, redesign, technology refresh, COTS replacement, alternate sourcing, last-time buys, and planned product transitions.
  • Conduct engineering trade studies to evaluate mitigation alternatives based on technical risk, lifecycle cost, schedule, performance, supportability, and future product needs.
  • Partner with the Chief Engineer to evaluate technical solutions and ensure proposed obsolescence mitigation strategies remain consistent with system architecture and future product evolution.
  • Advocate for commercially available, off-the-shelf (COTS) solutions over proprietary designs where technically and commercially appropriate to improve sustainability, flexibility, and lifecycle cost.
  • Provide data-driven technical inputs to product roadmaps, ROMs, BOEs, proposals, sustainment planning, and investment decisions.
  • Collaborate with Systems, Electrical, Mechanical, Software, Test, Product Management, Program Management, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to develop and execute approved mitigation strategies.
  • Coordinate with suppliers and external obsolescence-management providers to support component monitoring, lifecycle analysis, alerts, and supply-chain risk identification.
  • Maintain awareness of industry trends, emerging technologies, supplier roadmaps, and supply-chain dynamics that may affect product longevity.

General Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Work cross-functionally with engineering, product management, program management, and supply chain teams.
  • Communicate obsolescence risks, trade-offs, and recommendations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Support long-term product sustainability, technology refresh, and modernization planning.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of engineering processes, tools, metrics, and reporting associated with obsolescence and lifecycle management.
  • Identify opportunities for common solutions and technology reuse across products where appropriate.
  • Maintain awareness of industry trends, emerging technologies, and supply chain dynamics impacting product longevity.

The description provided above is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all job duties, responsibilities and requirements. Duties, responsibilities and requirements may change over time and according to business need.


Minimum Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electronics Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • 8-12+ years of engineering experience involving complex, multidisciplinary systems, including experience in systems engineering, hardware/software development, product

sustainment, DMSMS/obsolescence management, technology refresh, or lifecycle management.

  • Strong systems engineering knowledge with demonstrated ability to understand complex systems consisting of hardware, software, firmware, networks, external interfaces, and supporting infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess how components or subsystem changes may affect requirements, interfaces, architecture, integration, verification, configuration, and overall system performance.
  • Experience working with complex integrated systems in defense, aerospace, simulation, training, communications, or similar environments.
  • Demonstrated understanding of component lifecycle management, DMSMS, supplier constraints, and supply-chain risk.
  • Experience conducting technical trade studies and evaluating alternatives based on technical performance, lifecycle cost, schedule, risk, and supportability.
  • Experience working across multiple engineering disciplines, products, or programs in a senior technical capacity.
  • Ability to analyze technical and lifecycle data and translate identified risks into actionable engineering recommendations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical issues and influence decisions across organizational boundaries.

Personal Qualities:

  • Strong systems thinker capable of understanding the relationship between component-level issues and overall system performance and supportability.
  • Technically curious and willing to investigate alternatives beyond traditional component replacement or last-time-buy approaches.
  • Execution-oriented with strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
  • Proactive and forward-looking, with the ability to identify emerging life-cycle risks before they become program or customer issues.
  • Able to develop technically defensible recommendations while recognizing that final technical and investment decisions reside with Engineering and Product Leadership.
  • Strong communicator capable of effectively collaborating across engineering disciplines, Product Management, Program Management, Supply Chain, and technical leadership.
  • Collaborative, accountable, and aligned with organizational goals.

Employee

jobs.excerpt: Packetlabs was built by an ethical hacker after seeing vulnerability assessments presented as penetration tests.
jobs.description:
Packetlabs was built by an ethical hacker after seeing vulnerability assessments presented as penetration tests. Our slogan "Identify Risks Before They Become Headlines" drives at the importance of not providing our clients with a false sense of security.

We’re hiring our founding Principal Software Engineer to help build Packetlabs’ internal application and platform frameworks from the ground up.

There’s no legacy system to inherit and no existing architecture to work around. You’ll make the first decisions from the cloud account structure, the repo and service layout, the identity model, the data model, the CI/CD and IaC foundations, and the standards every engineer after you will build on.

We need someone who can hold two horizons at once. You’ll ship the initial setups our consultants need now, while designing them to support where Packetlabs is headed: more services, more clients, more automation, more engineers, and new products we haven’t built yet. You’ll work directly with leadership to understand where the business is going and translate that into a technical plan and roadmap.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with real authority. You’ll make the foundational decisions on architecture, standards, and tooling, then write the code that proves them out.

Who we are looking for

  • Core Values:
    • You’ve built something from zero before, such as a platform, a product, or an engineering function, and you want to do it again.
    • You’re energized by a blank page, not intimidated by it. You can create structure where none exists.
    • You naturally ask “what happens when we’re 5x bigger?” and design the answer into the foundation, without over-engineering for a future that may not come.
    • You know which decisions are expensive to change later, such as identity, tenancy, data models, account structure, and core abstractions. You get those right early and stay flexible on the rest.
    • You’re comfortable wearing many hats early on: architect, developer, DBA, DevOps, and sometimes product manager.
    • You can turn business strategy into technical strategy, and explain technical trade-offs in business terms.
  • Education and Experience:
    • Required
      • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant time owning architecture for production systems.
      • Proven experience building a platform, product, or engineering foundation from scratch.
      • A track record of making architectural decisions that held up as the business and team grew.
      • Experience creating technical roadmaps tied to business goals and communicating them to non-technical leadership.
      • Production AWS and infrastructure-as-code experience with Pulumi and/or Terraform, including designing reusable modules and multi-environment strategy.
      • Experience with delegated and application-wide implementation of OAuth and ReBac authorization strategies across users, service accounts, and API keys
      • Strong database design and administration skills, especially with PostgreSQL: data modelling, performance tuning, migrations, and backup and recovery.
      • Experience designing and operating CI/CD pipelines with automated testing and security gates.
      • Strong working knowledge of identity protocols and patterns: OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, federation, and service-to-service auth.
      • Proficiency in Python, and TypeScript, working across the frontend and backend stack (e.g., React, Node) and comfort with solving problems in other programming languages.
    • Nice To Have
      • Experience at a security company, or building security tooling (scanners, ASM/CTEM, vulnerability management, reporting platforms).
      • Familiarity with offensive security workflows and tools (Burp Suite, Nmap, Nuclei, and the like), or a background in penetration testing or AppSec.
      • Experience with workflow orchestration engines, frameworks and architecture
      • Experience building production AI/LLM features.
      • Experience supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 programs.
      • Security certifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

What you’ll be doing

  • You’ll architect and build the platforms that power Packetlabs’ offensive security operations. These include internal systems for our consultants and operations teams, and client-facing products.

Architecture and technical vision

    • Define and own the end-to-end architecture across applications, services, data, and infrastructure.
    • Work with leadership to turn the business’s growth plans into a multi-year technical vision and roadmap.
    • Design core abstractions such as identity, tenancy, data models, and eventing to scale with new service lines, clients, and products.
    • Make deliberate build-vs-buy and technology decisions, and document them so the reasoning outlives the decision.

Platform foundations

    • Stand up the company’s engineering foundations from the ground up: frameworks, cloud environments (AWS), CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi/Terraform), and observability.
    • Architect identity and access for staff, consultants, and clients, including SSO, federation, and multi-tenant authorization (RBAC/ReBac).
    • Own data architecture and database strategy, keeping sensitive client data secure, isolated, and well governed.

Orchestration and automation

    • Architect a scalable orchestration platform that runs security tooling, tracks assets, and turns raw results into high-quality findings.
    • Design workflows that connect the full engagement lifecycle, from scoping and testing through reporting, delivery, and retesting.
    • Identify where automation and AI can make consultants faster and more effective.

Engineering standards and team growth

    • Set the standards for how we build, ship, and operate software, including a secure SDLC built in from day one.
    • Create golden paths and reusable patterns so new applications and services launch quickly and consistently.
    • Plan the growth of the engineering function: who to hire next, how teams own services, and how to bring penetration testers and operators into product development.
    • Mentor engineers and partner with practice leads to turn operational needs into platform capabilities.

Why us?

  • Build the platform for a firm that takes offensive security seriously, with users (our consultants) who’ll give you sharp, honest feedback.
  • A true ground-floor opportunity to shape the architecture, standards, and engineering culture from day one.
  • A leadership team that values substance, quality, and disciplined execution.
  • Collaboration with a highly skilled team of security professionals who are passionate about technical excellence.
  • Competitive compensation and growth opportunity
  • GRSP with corporate matching in Canada
  • Participation in corporate benefit plans within Canada
  • A flexible work environment that empowers you to do your best work
  • Fully remote within Canada

This role will own and execute AI Platform strategy, defining the multi-year roadmap, cross-service-line capability, and coherence that position the platform as a strategic asset, scaling to 1,000 deployed AI agents across every solution, from intelligent tax preparation to agentic audit workflows. The role will build model lifecycle, evaluation, and multi-vendor orchestration as usage expands across every team.

What Work You Will be Responsible For:

Own and Execute AI Platform Strategy

  • Own the multi-year platform roadmap — architecture, model lifecycle, and governance-as-code — scaling the EisnerAI Platform on Azure toward 1,000+ deployed agents while ensuring Tax, Audit, Advisory, and Outsourcing build on one coherent foundation.

  • Define and enforce model lifecycle standards (active, legacy, deprecated, retired) and evaluation benchmarks across the firm's multi-LLM environment, turning vendor and model choices — GPT-4o, o3, and what comes next, into a deliberate portfolio strategy rather than ad hoc adoption.
